Asmasael.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Librarian]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[Chapter]].{{Fn|1}}

During the [[Diamor Campaign]], he worked closely alongside [[Captain]] [[Aphael]] in fighting the [[Black Legion]], [[Crimson Slaughter]], [[Butcherhorde]], and [[Word Bearers]]. However after the [[Chaos Lord]] [[Xorphas]] completed his ritual with the [[Banshee Stone]] on [[Amethal]], Asmasael sent a distress call to [[Titan (Moon)|Titan]] to request aid from the [[Grey Knights]]{{Fn|1}}. In the aftermath of the ritual's completion, Asmasael managed to destroy the source of the Chaos disturbance - the Banshee Stone - and stopped the appearance of a [[Warp Rift]] on Amethal, though only for some time{{Fn|2}}. During the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]], he was still on Amethal, guarding the site where the Chaos ritual took place, when [[Daemonic]] incursions struck the worlds of the [[Diamor System]]. As Amethal began to be overrun, the Librarian sent a desperate message to [[Baal]] asking for more reinforcements, but was denied as the Baal System was now threatened by incoming [[Tyranid]] [[Hive Fleet]]s. Asmasael replied that he understood and asked that the souls of the Blood Angels fighting in the Diamor System be commended to their [[Primarch]] [[Sanguinius]], before going to defend Amethal. He received multiple messages afterwards telling him to abandon Amethal, with whatever resources he could recover, and return to Baal immediately, but Asmasael does not or cannot reply to them.{{Fn|3}}

(Formerly){{Fn|4}} *Master [[Interrogator-Chaplain]] of the [[Dark Angels]].{{Fn|2}} |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Dark Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Asmodai''' is a '''Master [[Interrogator-Chaplain]]''' of the [[Dark Angels]]. One of the oldest and most successful Interrogator-Chaplains in the Chapter's history, he is also renowned as one of the most dark and sinister members of the [[Unforgiven]]. Suspected [[Fallen]] have learned that it is better to die than to fall into Asmodai's hands.{{Fn|2}} ===Biography=== Asmodai was a well-regarded but unremarkable [[Tactical Marine]] serving in the Dark Angels' [[8th Company (Dark Angels)|8th Company]] in 405.[[M41]] during the [[Macharian Heresy]]. During the battle of Hive-Moon Sigma, Asmodai fought under [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Elijah (Master)|Elijah]] against the rebellious forces of the [[Dark Angel]] [[Malvine Rhemell]]. During the fight the Dark Angels took heavy losses and Rhemell escaped, and Asmodai vowed to find him and make him repent. Afterwards he was quickly elevated to the position of Interrogator-Chaplain and captured his first Fallen Angel, [[Cephesus (Asmodai)|Cephesus]], in 411.[[M41]], though he failed to make him repent. Over the next 25 years he captured three more, but they, too, refused to repent. Asmodai, however, had his first success after forcing the Fallen Angel [[Sorl Mebbon]] to repent after 18 days of torture. Asmodai quickly gained a reputation for ruthless and uncompromising dedication.{{Fn|4}} In his long career, he has only been able to make two members of [[The Fallen]] repent. But not many can resist his evil craft, and it is said that his enemies would rather die than fall into his hands, as he is rumoured to be able to keep a victim alive for weeks on end while undergoing horrific torture.{{Fn|1}} Such is Asmodai's brutality and excess that even [[Azrael]] has had to counteract and cover up his actions multiple times over the Chapter's history.{{Fn|3}} [[File:Asmodaiart.jpg|thumb|Asmodai artwork]] It was Asmodai who ordered the slaughter of all the new recruits from [[Narcium]] because of their lacklustre answers to his questions. Upon hearing laughter in the halls of [[The Rock]], Asmodai placed the penance of silence upon the entire [[7th Company (Dark Angels)|7th Company]]. However, despite his brutal and disciplinary streaks, he is nonetheless an effective combatant and inspiring leader. He famously led the Dark Angels against the traitors of [[Rhun's Palace]] and inspired an impressive stand when his forces were surrounded by [[Daemons]] on the world of [[Amity]].{{Fn|3}} As with all Interrogator-Chaplains, he carries a weapon known as the [[Blades of Reason]], a device used to inflict torment.{{Cite this}} ====Pandorax Campaign==== *{{Main|Pandorax Campaign}} {{Spoiler|source=Pandorax (Novel)}} In 960.[[M41]] Asmodai fought in the [[Pandorax Campaign]]; he was part of a boarding assault on the [[asteroid]] [[Malefus Murex]] along with other elements of the chapter when they entered the [[Pandorax System|system]].{{Fn|7a}} At the end of the campaign [[Balthasar]] brought [[Corpulax]] before [[Azrael]], [[Gabriel (Dark Angels)|Gabriel]], and Asmodai, offering him as a prisoner for Asmodai, in response Asmodai activated his [[Crozius]]. He listened to Corpulax's speech then laughed at him with the other Dark Angels present, and watched as Balthasar executed him on Azrael's command.{{Fn|7b}} Later onboard [[The Rock]], Asmodai and Gabriel met Balthasar as he arrived after the campaign, leading him away to tell him more of the Dark Angels' secrets.{{Fn|7c}} ====Arks of Omen==== *{{Main|Arks of Omen Campaign}} During the Siege of [[The Rock]] during the [[Arks of Omen Campaign]], {{PAGENAME}} took part in the defence of their Fortress-Monastery against [[Chaos]] forces. In the Vault of Banners Asmodai and over 50 battle brothers fought off 4 waves of attackers before launching a counterattack that caused the remainder to flee.{{Fn|5a}} He would then lead elements of [[4th Company (Dark Angels)|4th]] and [[5th Company (Dark Angels)|5th company]] in a counter-assault against [[Gar Hathon]] and the [[Word Bearers]] in the silent sanctum.{{Fn|5b}} After the battle, Asmodai oversaw the interrogation and capture of captured [[Chaos Space Marine]]s to learn of [[Vashtorr]]'s next move.{{Fn|5c}} Shortly thereafter Vashtorr was identified as dwelling within the [[Somnium Stars]], and Asmodai led Unforgiven forces in the [[Battle of Idolatros]].{{Fn|6}} ==Wargear== Asmodai goes into battle with the ancient [[Crozius Arcanum]] ''[[Censure (Crozius)|Censure]]'' and the [[Power Sword]] ''[[Catechist]]''. He also wields the infamous [[Blades of Reason]] for both interrogation and combat.{{Fn|8}} ===Images=== Asmodai.jpg|Asmodai miniature ([[2nd Edition]]) M2860209a 99800101056 Asmodai01 873x627.jpg|Asmodai miniature ([[6th Edition]]) Asmodai2024.jpg|Asmodai miniature ([[10th Edition]]) ===Trivia=== {{Trivia}} *Asmodai is named after a King of Demons known by the same name (but usually referred to as Asmodeus) who is the primary antagonist of the ''"Book of Tobit"'' from the Bible, as well as being featured in several earlier Hebrew texts, and later Christian texts. He is one of the Seven Princes of Hell, representing Lust. ===See also=== *[[List of Chaplains]] ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[White Dwarf 266 (UK)]] {{Cite this}} *{{Endn|2}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/gws/catalog/productDetail.jsp?catId=cat440160a&prodId=prod1830086a Games Workshop] *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Dark Angels (6th Edition)]], pg. 77 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Warlords of the Dark Millennium: Asmodai (Background Book)]] *5: [[Arks of Omen: Vashtorr]]: **{{Endn|5a}}: pg. 19 **{{Endn|5b}}: pg. 21 **{{Endn|5c}}: pg. 31 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Arks of Omen: The Lion]], pg. 14 *{{Endn|7}}: [[Pandorax (Novel)]] **{{Endn|7a}}: Chapter 9 **{{Endn|7b}}: Chapter 15 **{{Endn|7c}}: Postlude *{{Endn|8}}: [[Codex Supplement: Dark Angels (10th Edition)]], pg. 25 ====Uncited==== {{Uncited}} *[[Codex: Dark Angels (3rd Edition)]] *[http://oz.games-workshop.com/games/40k/spacemarines/catalog/darkangels/asmodai.htm Asmodai page from Games Workshop OZ] {{DAForces}} [[Category:Characters (Dark Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Space Marine Chaplains)]] [[de:Asmodai]] [[fr:Asmodai]]

Assumpta.wikitext:
{{AdeptaSororitasPortal}}
'''Assumpta''' is a [[Battle Sister]] of the [[Order of the Bloody Rose]] who, in the aftermath of the [[Great Rift|Great Rift's]] creation, was struck by a divine vision as she was aboard a fleet of ships, containing multiple Preceptories of the Order, that was en route to the [[Realm of Ultramar]].

Her vision showed her the lone world in the [[Thresh System]] and, though Assumpta had yet to see combat, the Preceptories' [[Canoness]]es took her vision seriously and the fleet was rerouted to the [[system]].  Once there, the Sisters deployed to the Thresh System's lone world and waited as the Canonessess prayed for guidance.  Their duty was then made clear to them, when a tendril of [[Ouroboros (Hive Fleet)|Hive Fleet Ouroboris]] appeared and was drawn to the Sisters' presence.  Great waves of [[Tyranid]]s then invaded the barren world and in the battle that followed, the Sisters denied the [[Xenos]] the chance to feed off any biomass, by burning the dead to ashes.  After six months of battle, the influx of Hive Fleet Ouroboris into the Thresh System ceased and six months later, the last of the [[Hive Fleet|Hive Fleet's]] Tyranids was finally killed.  Assumpta was the only member of the Bloody Rose Preceptories to survive the fierce battle.{{Fn|1}}

'''Aster Crohne''', known as the '''Ghost of Saiph'''{{Fn|3}}, was a [[Centurion (Rank)|Centurion]] in the [[Blood Angels]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion's]] [[94th Company (Blood Angels Legion)|94th Company]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
A veteran of the Blood Angels, Crohne served in the Legion in the days before the coming of [[Sanguinius]].  Recruited from the killing fields of [[Saiph]], as a child, it is said none survived as many massacres and slaughters of Aster Crohne.  He was among the few of his tribe from the wastes of his homeworld to survive recruitment into the Legion.  He became known for his survival skills and bloody-minded tenacity that defied belief even within the IXth Legion.  Upon the coming of Sanguinius and the reformation of the Legion from a force of bloodthirsty killers to that of noble warriors, Crohne was seen as a relic and garnered little favor from the new elite of his Legion, lingering as the rank of [[Centurion (Rank)|Judiciar]].{{Fn|1c}} Despite Crohne's faithful service, Sanguinius came to lament the inclusion of the Saiph-born Blood Angels into his now enlightened [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]].{{Fn|3}}

He later became the 94th Company's brevetted commander{{Fn|1a}}, after [[Praetor (Rank)|Archein]] [[Malaci]] was killed in the [[Inconnu Campaign]]{{Fn|1b}} and, due to no replacement having been chosen, Crohne led the Company in the [[Battle of Signus Prime]].{{Fn|1a}}  During the war on Signus he was one of the few Blood Angels to maintain his sanity and not succumb to the [[Red Thirst]].  Despite this, he remained an outcast among his peers, a symbol of the failings of the Blood Angels during Signus.{{Fn|1c}}

Aster Crohne later returned in 013.[[M31]] to take part in a raid on Traitor-occupied [[Mars]] at [[Sanguinius]]' orders. [[Schism of Mars_#The Arca Silentus|Leading the 94th Company against Lukas Chrom's scrap code beacon on Mars]], Crohne was badly wounded by a [[Brass Scorpion]] but was successful in destroying the beacon. His fate afterwards is unknown.{{Fn|2}}

===Wargear===
Crohne wielded the [[power axe]] known as the [[Saiphan Shard-axe]].{{Fn|3}}

Asterion Moloc.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}
[[Image:MolocArt.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Asterion Moloc]]
'''Asterion Moloc''' — '''Satrap of the ''[[Daedelos Krata]]''''', '''Bringer of Wrath''', the '''Brazen Warlord''', '''Spear of Judgement''' — is the current [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Minotaurs]]. Bloody-handed and paranoid, he is a dark legend whose name is a byword for destruction and slaughter in the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor's]] name.{{Fn|2}}

==Biography==
A diligent and disciplined logistician, strategist, and  master of siegecraft, Lord Asterion Moloc revels in his dark reputation. The veteran of a hundred battles, his body has been heavily rebuilt with cybernetic augments and his sheer spite and malice are enough to allow him to shrug off wounds that would fell a lesser Space Marine. Moloc takes pleasure in the utter destruction of his foes, most often found in battle at the head of his Terminators slamming into the enemy line, and has personally slain several renegade [[Chapter Master|Chapter Masters]], as well as [[Ork]] [[Warboss|Warbosses]], [[Eldar Corsairs|Corsair Princes]], and [[Champion of Chaos|Champions]] of the [[Chaos Gods|Dark Gods]].{{Fn|2}}. Outside of battle, he can be found on his brazen throne at the center of the maze-like chambers of the heavy assault carrier ''[[Daedelos Krata]]'', surrounded by data-feeds, tabulation servitors, and casualty reports, measuring the drops of blood spilt in quest of his Chapter's strategic goals.{{fn|1}}

The Minotaurs Chapter have been used often in the past to persecute traitors, iconoclasts, and renegades from within the ranks of the Space Marines by the [[High Lords of Terra]]. As a result, Asterion Moloc has long become expert in the systematic destruction of other Adeptus Astartes forces that have strayed from the path of righteousness, viewing such targets as both worthy of the Emperor's wrath, and the ultimate test of the Minotaurs' skills in battle. This reason above any other was the one of the fundamental causes for the Minotaurs Chapter to join the Loyalists in the [[Badab War]] and many of their battles, specifically the savage engagements in which they devastated the [[Lamenters]] Chapter and forced their surrender, having entered into legend among the Space Marines{{Fn|1}}.

Asterion Moloc was the commander-in-chief of the Space Marine forces sent to the [[Amarah]] system by request of governor [[Calibron Laan]] to defend it against an unknown enemy. During the [[Orphean War#The Battle of Amarah|Amarah Void Battle]], Moloc led an assault force into the heart of the [[Necron]] vessel ''Dead Hand'' and fought with the [[Necron Overlord]] believed to be [[Maktlan Kutlakh]], war leader of the [[Maynarkh]], before he was vented into space, badly wounded. Moloc was initially reported as killed in action, but his fleet recovered him alive. This is at least the seventh such incident over the last five centuries, which leads some to believe that "Asterion Moloc" is a legacy inherited by the Chapter Master of the Minotaurs along with his panoply and engrammatically-enforced memories and personality{{Fn|2}}.

During the [[Age of the Dark Imperium]] Moloc arrived at [[Terra]] with the rest of his Chapter, proclaiming his Chapter had escaped [[Death Guard]] assault but in truth due to the [[Hexarchy]]'s plans. He oversaw the Minotaurs' anti-cultist activities on Terra, with his brutal scorched-earth tactics putting him into conflict with [[Tor Garadon]], [[Trajann Valoris]], and [[Violeta Roskavler]].{{Fn|3a}} When the Hexarchy's coup collapsed due to the betrayal of [[Fadix]] and a counterattack by [[Custodes]] and [[Imperial Fists]], Moloc prepared his chapter to fight. However he was confronted by Violeta Roskavler, now the sole claimant of [[Master of the Administratum]] due to the fight of [[Irthu Haemotalion]]. Curiously, Moloc promptly withdrew the Minotaurs from Terra after Roskavler whispered something in his ear.{{Fn|3b}}

==Wargear==
Moloc wears an ornate suit of [[Terminator Armour#Tartaros Pattern|Tartaros Pattern Terminator Armor]] into battle. He wields the [[Black Spear]], a truly deadly relic-weapon of unknown provenance that is similar in some regards to weapons of the [[Adeptus Custodes]], and carries a heraldic [[storm shield]] marked with archaic [[Terra]]n Helac glyphs of unknown significance.{{fn|2}}

("Father" via [[Gene-Seed]]) |Occupation =[[High Chaplain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Blood Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Astorath''', known as '''Astorath the Grim''', is the [[High Chaplain]] of the [[Blood Angels]].{{Fn|1a}} == History == Astorath is a figure both revered and loathed within the ranks of the Chapter due to the duty he performs: as the Redeemer of the Lost, he must seek out those battle-brothers completely claimed by the [[Black Rage]], and end their suffering with a blow from his axe. As a result no battle-brother can feel entirely comfortable in his presence, as one day it might be their neck at the receiving end of his blade.{{Fn|1a}} [[Image:AstorathArt.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Astorath the Grim]] While his duties ultimately lie with his Chapter, Astorath also dispenses the final mercy of oblivion to those lost to the Rage in all Blood Angel [[Successor]] Chapters. As such he is always on the move, his grim duty bringing him to wherever the [[Sanguinary Brotherhood|Sons of Sanguinius]] battle.{{Fn|1a}} A less-keen observer might mistake Astorath's presence on the battlefield as actually exacerbating the Black Rage in his brothers, but the truth is actually quite the opposite; Astorath can ''sense'' the onset of the Black Rage in brother Marines before any visible signs manifest, and as such appears on those forlorn battlefields where he fights to lead these doomed individuals in one last glorious charge before the Flaw completely overtakes their sanity.{{Fn|1a}} Upon the introduction of [[Primaris Space Marine]]s into the [[Chapter]] following the [[Devastation of Baal]], Astorath was always skeptical that these new recruits would be immune to the [[Red Thirst]] and [[Black Rage]] despite the initial rumors.{{Fn|3a}} Sure enough, the Chaplain was proven correct. It soon became time for Astorath to grant the gift of mercy to fallen Primaris intended for the [[Red Wings]] Chapter.{{Fn|3b}} ==Wargear== Astorath is armed with the [[Executioner's Axe]], a two-handed [[Power Axe]] so keen it could slice through power fields, and is clad in crimson-coloured [[Artificer Armour]] equipped with a black-winged [[Jump Pack]]. {{OrdoHereticusPortal}}
[[Image:AstridSkane.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Inquisitor Astrid Skane{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Astrid Skane''' is an [[Ordo Hereticus]] [[Inquisitor]] of the [[Radical]] [[Recongregator]] faith, who is active in the [[Calixis Sector]].{{Fn|1}} 

She was formally an [[Adeptus Arbites]] [[Judge]], who rooted out a series of [[Slaanesh|pleasure]] [[Chaos Cult|Cults]] amongst the [[Noble House|nobility]] of [[Scintilla]]’s [[Hive]]s. At that time, Skane had found herself fighting a lonely battle against adversaries wielding power both political and martial, but she persevered in her task. Skane's success (with the aid from several allies of the [[Inquisition]]'s [[Tricorn Palace]]) saw her become famous amongst the [[Calixis Sector]]'s [[Holy Ordos]]. This led her to be inducted into the ranks of the [[Ordo Calixis]] as an [[Acolyte]] and eventually Skane was elevated to the status of [[Inquisitor]].{{Fn|2}} 

She now serves in the [[Ordo Hereticus]] and has become a [[Recongregator]], who dreams of a future where justice in the [[Imperium]] is a rule rather than the exception. Skane also believes that the [[Tyrant Star]]'s appearance, is due to some sort of [[Cult]] activity.{{Fn|1}}

{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
[[Image:Astrovel.jpg|thumb|right|Astrovel{{Fn|2}}]]
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the Fourth [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Dark Angels]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s Seventh Order during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Perditus]], he was assigned by his [[Primarch]] [[Lion El'Jonson]] to a strike force, led by Seneschal [[Corswain]], that was charged with both hunting down the fleeing [[Death Guard]] forces of [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Typhus]] and to bring word of the battle to the [[Space Wolves]] Legion's [[Primarch]] [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]]. However, after many months, the strike force could not find any trace of Leman Russ, and as for Typhus, they found only worlds that were left in disarray or that had been destroyed by his touch. During one of the many war councils between the strike force's commanders, unrest began to show about their lack of progress and Astrovel voiced that they should instead return to [[Caliban]] and increase its defenses. After much arguing, it was finally decided that the strike force would be split off by Orders, each with their own goals to pursue. Corswain would go with Chapter Master [[Belath]]'s Second Order to continue pursuing Typhus, while the other Orders would travel to nearby [[System]]s to search for the Primarch Leman Russ and to attack any Traitors they came across.{{Fn|1}}

He was the founder of the [[Path of the Warrior]] and he created the first shrine of [[Asur]], the [[Dire Avenger]] shrine, which was to grow into the most wide-spread of the [[Aspect]]s. Asurmen's name means ''"The Hand of [[Asuryan]]"'' and it was he who led the Eldar race away from their doomed homeworlds at the time of the [[Fall of the Eldar]]. ==Biography== [[Image:Asurmen Art.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Asurmen{{Fn|7}}]] Born '''Iliathin''', the Eldar who would become Asurmen was born on the world of [[Eidafaeron]] and lived an uneventful and boring life there. Before the [[Fall of the Eldar]], he was skeptical of the prophecies of doom being spread by those who would become the [[Exodite]]s. Iliathin's brother [[Tethesis]] wanted to join the Exodites but his skeptical sibling refuses to take part. Once the Doom of the Eldar came, Ilaithin and his brother both somehow survived the calamity and waged a desperate struggle for survival amid the ruins of their world, now overrun with [[Daemon]]s. When Tethesis was possessed by a Daemon, Iliathin was forced to kill him. Afterwards, he managed to find shelter at an old temple which Daemons do not venture near due to the lingering presence of the [[Eldar God]]s.{{Fn|5}} Contemplating suicide, Iliathin lived alone in the temple for several years but was saved by an Eldar feral child [[Jain Zar|Faraethil]]. Though initially shunning the girl, later when Faraethil was assaulted by [[Dark Eldar]], Iliathin renamed himself '''Asurmen''' after the god [[Asuryan]] and saved her. Asurmen agreed to take the girl as his disciple and they left the planet, eventually gathering more like-minded followers.{{Fn|5}} Asurmen and his followers landed on a barren world and renamed it [[Asur]]. There, he founded the first of the Aspect shrines, the Dire Avengers, which have become the most common of all the warrior Aspects.{{Fn|1a}} Asurmen established the [[Asurya]], who went on to open new Aspect Shrines across the stars.{{Fn|2}} He has traveled to more [[craftworld]]s than any other Phoenix Lord, teaching those Eldar who wanted to learn, and has founded more shrines than any other Phoenix Lord. The greatest of his students went on to found their own Aspect shrines and became Phoenix Lords themselves.{{Fn|1a}} Soon after the inception of the Aspect Shrines, the Hand of Asuryan vanished, but tales of his deeds continue to be reported. Experiencing various deaths but being reborn again thanks to his armor, notably at the hands of the [[Keeper of Secrets]] [[N'Kari]]{{Fn|3}}, he has been rumored slaying the agents of [[Chaos]] in the [[Eye of Terror]] to the [[Eastern Fringe]]. His actions have even become legends to the lesser races.{{Fn|2}} Asurmen later appeared under the command of [[Jain Zar]], now pledged to [[Ynnead]]. Asurmen took part in the battle to defend the [[Ynnari]] against the [[Thousand Sons]] and [[Tzeentch]] [[Daemon]]s in the [[Webway]], vanishing during the struggle.{{Fn|6}} ==Wargear== Asurmen's ancient armour incorporates vambraces with integrated [[Shuriken Catapults]] known as the ''[[Bloody Twins]]'' and his [[Diresword]] (named [[The Sword of Asur]]{{Fn|4}}) was the first created and contained the spirit of his brother, [[Tethesis]], who was slain by a [[Daemon]].{{Fn|1a}} Asurmen is capable of navigating the [[Webway]] thanks to his ship, the ''[[Stormlance]]''. ==Images== Asurmen.jpg|Asurmen Miniature (2nd Edition){{Fn|1b}} Asurmen10th.jpg|Asurmen Miniature (10th Edition){{Fn|8}} YinYang.jpg|The ancient rune of Asurmen ==See also== *[[Phoenix Lord]] ==Source== *1: [[Codex: Eldar (4th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: pg. 55 **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 79 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Codex: Eldar (6th Edition)]] (E-Book), pg. 88 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Iyanden: A Codex: Eldar Supplement]] (E-Book), pg. 83 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Craftworlds (7th Edition)]] (e-book), ''Asurmen - Atarine Hestia.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a veteran [[Sister of Silence]] who established an enclave of the Sisterhood on the [[Imperium]] world [[Arraissa]] in late [[M41]]. 

By that time the Sisters of Silence had long lost their standing among the other militant orders of the Imperium and were largely ignored and forgotten. This had caused the Sisterhood's Order to fragment and led to the formations of many isolated enclaves, who still served the [[Emperor]] to the best of their ability. Hestia's enclave was one of these isolated Sisterhoods, but she was able to keep the enclave supplied with equipment, staff to aid the Sisters in their mission and pay the necessary tithes and bribes to keep the leadership of Arraissa away from them. Despite focusing on training new generations of Sisters of Silence, Hestia's skills remained sharp and she continued to hunt down the forces of [[Chaos]]. One such act, was during the early years of the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]], when Hestia single handedly destroyed the [[Circlet]] [[Cult]] in the shipyards of [[Eyrinan V]] and afterwards discovered information that led to several other Cults and Cultists{{Fn|1a}}. It was during the Crusade's fifth year, however that her years of service to the Emperor seemed to come to an end, when the [[Black Legion]] invaded Arraissa, in an attempt to end the threat the Sisters posed to them. When the attack was over, the enclave was destroyed and the Sisters and staff who supported them were killed. One of Hestia's disciples, the [[Witch Seeker]] [[Tanau Aleya]], later returned to the enclave, having been off-world when the attack occurred, and searched its wreckage for any survivors. While she did not find anyone alive within her former home, Aleya also did not find Hestia's body and refused to believe her skilled master met her end in the Black Legion's attack{{Fn|1b}}. Though she does not know what happened to Hestia, Aleya was sure she would meet her master again.{{Fn|1a}}

'''Atharva''' was an Adeptus Exemptus of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion|legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]].

===Biography===
====Morningstar====
During the 55th year of the Great Crusade, Atharva served on the planet [[Morningstar (Planet)|Morningstar]], where he tried to find out what led to the destruction of the pre-[[Old Night]] city of [[Zharrukin]]. When a magna-storm threatened the site, he ordered the evacuation with [[Conservator]] [[Niko Ashkali]], an academic leading the human staff. Using his telepathic powers, he summoned the other legionaries to leave, including [[Phosis T'kar]], but they were unable to reach [[Magnus]]. Waiting for the [[primarch]] caused them precious time, and one of the human transports was almost downed in the storm as it tried to take off. With T'kar, Atharva was able to use his power to save the ship and send it away from the storm. Knowing not much time was left, Atharva left his [[stormbird]] and ordered the legionaries to return to [[Calaena]] as he was going to find the primarch on his own. However, they stayed as Atharva ventured into the storm, but he did not have to go far when he met the primarch, whose psychic power kept the storm away. With the primarch on board, the pilot Zharrukin struggled to keep it flying through the storm. Before they could be lost, Magnus used his power again to protect the ship to the awe of the legionaries who were just beginning to learn of their primarch's power.{{Fn|2b}}

When they arrived at Calaena, Morningstar's capital city, they found a thriving trade hub that was busy evacuating civilians aboard the ancient mass convoyer, ''[[Lux Ferem]]''. The stormbird traveled to the [[Sharei Maveth]] fortress, built and manned by the Iron Warriors. Once landed, Magnus ordered Atharva to join him to meet with [[Perturabo]]. The two primarchs came together, with Perturabo expressing happiness at Magnus's safety, and Magnus revealing that he discovered something important, as Atharva watched in amazement that two very different individuals could be brothers Yet he saw that they were similar in their quest of knowledge and creating great wonders. As he gazed at Perturabo's armor, the primarch questioned him as to what he saw, and Atharva replied that the [[Terminator Armour|Terminator plate]] had unique aspects, including aspects related to the [[Terrawatt Clan]] armorers, the [[Narodnyan]] craft, and the [[Kholat Syakhl]] forges along with [[Ur-Phoenicia]]n script running across it. Perturabo turned his attention to Magnus, who revealed that they discovered sealed archives that could explain how Morningstar was able to survive relatively intact during the Old Night.{{Fn|2b}}

====Crusader Host====
Atharva lived on [[Terra]] due to being part of the [[Crusader Host]], where one member from each legion was placed on Terra to represent their legion on the birth world of the [[Imperium]]. Atharva represented the Thousand Son's presence on Terra.{{Fn|1a}}

====Horus Heresy====
{{Spoiler|source=The Outcast Dead (Novel)}}
After the Horus Heresy broke out 14 legionaries of the known 9 traitor [[Astartes]] Legions were imprisoned in the [[Khangba Marwu]] for their legions' crimes.{{Fn|1b}} These arrests were at the hand of the [[Preceptory]] with a force led by [[Nagasena]] and [[General]] [[Golovko]] of the [[Black Sentinels]].{{Fn|1a}} Atharva used his psychic powers to cause the human guards to rebel against the two [[Custodians]] and then broken himself and 6 of the other legionaries from the prison. During their escape, they took [[Kai Zulane]], an [[astropath]], with them. This astropath was currently under psychic interrogation by the hand of the Imperium, who wanted to unlock the secret knowledge placed within his mind by Magnus the Red. Atharva had the same goal, and he wanted to use the information.{{Fn|1b}}

====Death====
Atharva was executed by [[Rogal Dorn]] using his own personalised [[bolt pistol]] after being cornered at the [[Temple of Woe]] during their attempted escape from Terra.{{Fn|1c}}

On the [[Planet of Sorcerers]], Atharva, or a shade of Atharva, appeared to Magnus as he brooded over his defeat at the hands of [[Russ]]. After some discussion, Atharva warned Magnus that the [[Chaos Gods|Warp Gods]] were not done with his legion, and he would need to seek help in cheating his fate with knowledge from their time at Morningstar during the Great Crusade.{{Fn|2a}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Salamanders]] [[Space Marine Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

===Biography===
Following the [[Battle of Nocturne]], Abidemi was among the three Salamanders to discover the reborn [[Vulkan]] at Mt. Deathfire alongside [[Barek Zytos]] and [[Igen Gargo]]. The three were named Vulkan's ''[[Draaksward]]'', his traveling companions on his journey through the [[Webway]] to [[Terra]]. Atok Abidemi, along with Vulkan and the rest of the Draaksward, eventually reached the [[Imperial Palace]] on Terra after an arduous journey.{{Fn|1}}

Later during the [[Siege of Terra]] Abidemi alongside his two battle-brothers moved to defend the Western Hemispheric region of the Palace walls from an attack by the [[Thousand Sons]]. During this time Abidemi began to have visions of a great drake fighting a crimson drake at the volcanoes of [[Nocturne]]. In the subsequent battle they were aided by [[Bodvar Bjarki]] and his pack of [[Space Wolves]], with Abidemi combining with the [[Rune Priest]] to summon both the powers of [[Fenris]] and Nocturne to seemingly drive back [[Magnus the Red]]. To save them both from overloading with power, Abidemi had to sever their psychic connection by cutting off Bjarki's arm.{{Fn|2}} 

Learning from [[Lemuel Gaumon|Promeus]] that their apparent defeat of the Thousand Sons attack had just been a ruse to allow Magnus and an entourage to infiltrate the Palace. The group confronted Magnus and the Thousand Sons before the [[Golden Throne]], and during the battle Zytos died to save [[Vulkan]] from the Crimson King. After the battle Abidemi and Gargo alongside Bjarki joined the group of [[Nathaniel Garro]] and [[Garviel Loken]].{{Fn|2a}}

Later during the final stages of the Siege, Abidemi stayed by Vulkan's side at the foot of the [[Golden Throne]] as the Emperor left it to assault the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''. As traitor forces begin to pound down the last door into the Throneroom, Abidemi sheds tears as he agrees with Vulkan that the time has come to activate the [[Talisman of Seven Hammers]] and deny the enemy the throneworld.{{Fn|4a}} However after hearing the message being broadcast across Terra by [[Actae]] that the Emperor still lived and fighting Horus, the activation is averted.{{Fn|4}}

===Wargear===
Abidemi wielded the massive [[Chainsword]] ''[[Draukoros]]'', which once belonged to First Captain [[Artellus Numeon]].{{Fn|2b}}

His callous execution rubbed Ahriman the wrong way and created some doubt towards his father.{{Fn|1b}}

Atreus (Chapter Ancient).wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Atreus'''  was a former [[Chapter Ancient]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]].{{Fn|3}}
==History==
Before becoming a [[Chapter Ancient]],{{Fn|3}} Atreus was a [[Tactical Marine]] in the [[Ultramarines]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]] and served in [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Octavian (Chapter Ancient)|Octavian]]'s{{Fn|1c}} "Swords of Judgment" squadron. They were known for receiving a collective total of fifteen [[Marksman's Honour]] badges, for their uncanny precision with ranged weaponry.{{Fn|2}}
===Battle for Macragge===
During the [[First Tyrannic War]]'s [[Battle for Macragge]], [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Octavian (Chapter Ancient)|Octavian]] led the "Swords of Judgment," against the [[Tyranids]] of [[Hive Fleet Behemoth]], to defend their [[Adeptus Astartes Homeworld|Homeworld]].{{Fn|1b}} As the battle raged, the [[Ultramarines]] received a distress call from the [[Imperial Navy Lieutenant]] [[Varras]]. The Tyranids had attacked his [[Imperial Lander]], but Varras had survived a crash landing onto [[Macragge]] and requested help from the [[Chapter]], as he carried one of their [[Gene-seed]] canisters. They would need to reach him quickly though, as the Lieutenant was fending off attacks by the [[Xenos]].{{Fn|1a}} Octavian's squadron was charged with rescuing Varras and the Gene-seed canister,{{Fn|1b}} but it would be split in half to complete their mission.{{Fn|1c}} One half would be led by the Sergeant and would be dropped off near the Lieutenant,{{Fn|1b}} while the other half would act as reinforcements and would be led by [[Atreus (Chapter Ancient)|Atreus]].{{Fn|1c}} Octavian's squadron soon successfully rescued Varras{{Fn|1d}} and was then reunited with Atreus' squadron. The Lieutenant and the "Swords of Judgment" then fought their way clear of the Tyranids and were evacuated by the [[Cestus]].{{Fn|1e}}

The squadron later aided the [[Ultramarines]] in defending part of a defensive cordon, that the [[Chapter]] had established against the [[Hive Fleet Behemoth]]. It was designed to prevent the [[Tyranids]] from gaining further access to [[Macragge]]'s surface, but the [[Xenos]] sent a large force to attack the cordon.{{Fn|1f}} This led Octavian's section to come under increasing pressure and an [[Assault Marine]] squadron, led by [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Furiae]], was sent to aid the beleaguered "Swords of Judgment". The two squads then worked together to combat the Tyranids and they then launched a successful counteroffensive, that regained the ground Octavian had lost to Hive Fleet Behemoth.{{Fn|1g}}

===Ichar IV Campaign===
During the [[Second Tyrannic War]]'s [[Ichar IV Campaign]], Atreus was the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chapter Ancient]], while [[Octavian (Chapter Ancient)|Octavian]] was its [[Chapter Champion]].{{Fn|3}} 

Sometime in late [[M41]], though, Atreus was killed in battle and [[Octavian (Chapter Ancient)|Octavian]] succeeded him as the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chapter Ancient]].{{Fn|3}}

'''Attias''', better known as '''Attias the Untamed''', is a notorious [[Fallen Angel]]{{Fn|1b}}, who took part{{Fn|2}} in the [[Great Crusade]]{{Fn|3}} and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|2}}


==Biography==
Once the trainee of [[Zahariel]] when he began with [[The Order]] on [[Caliban]], he was considered more of a bookworm than a fighter, until his successful ascension alongside his mentor to the [[Dark Angels]].{{Fn|4a}} In the First Legion's [[Battle of Sarosh|Sarosh campaign]], he was heavily injured by a xenos,{{Fn|4b}} and in the aftermath he was among the Dark Angels exiled back to [[Caliban]] by their [[Primarch]], [[Lion El'Jonson]].{{Fn|3}}

Said to have been at [[Luther]]'s side during the confrontation between the [[Fallen Angel|Fallen]] and [[Lion El'Jonson]], Attias has eluded capture by the [[Dark Angels]] over three times. However, at some point he became a captive of the [[Crimson Slaughter]], who attempted to use the Fallen as bait to lure the Dark Angels into a trap on the [[Imperial]] world of [[Stern's Remembrance]]. In the ensuing ambush, Attias was freed and fought alongside the Dark Angels, agreeing to become their prisoner if it meant freedom from the vile [[Chaos Space Marines]]. After the battle against the Crimson Slaughter and their [[Cultist]] allies, he was taken aboard [[The Rock]].{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}}

Augusta Santorus.wikitext:
{{AdeptaSororitasPortal}}
'''Augusta Santorus''' is a [[Sister Superior]] and twenty year veteran of the [[Order of the Bloody Rose]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
===Lautius===
[[Image:RoseAtWarCover.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Sister Augusta Santorus{{Fn|6}}]]
When the [[Missionary]] [[Lysimachus Tanichus]] sent word to [[Ophelia VII]] about possibly discovering an ancient cathedral dedicated to [[Saint]] [[Mina]] on [[Lautis]], Augusta immediately volunteered to discover the truth of the matter. She was told, however, that Lautis had been out of contact with the [[Imperium]] for millennia, until Tanichus arrived to reconvert them to the [[Imperial Cult]]. Though the world could have now potentially become a staging area for the forces of [[Chaos]] or [[Xenos]], Augusta was determined to find out if Saint Mina once walked its surface. However, as her squadron and Tanichus searched the cathedral for evidence of the Saint's presence, they soon discovered that a large [[Ork]] horde was approaching it. Augusta, was unwilling to abandon the holy site to the [[Xenos]] and both her squadron and Tanichus opened fire upon the Orks. With the element of surprise, many of the Orks fell, before the Xenos finally swarmed the cathedral.{{Fn|1}} 

In the fierce fighting that followed, Augusta clashed with the horde's [[Warboss]], but the [[Xenos]] managed to grab hold of her. She was then shocked, when the brute laughed and told her the Orks had known the Sisters would be in the cathedral. Before the Warboss could kill Augusta, however, her [[Battle Sister]] [[Viola]] pointed her [[bolter]] at the Ork and ordered him to put the [[Sister Superior]] down. The Warboss paused and it was then he discovered that his horde had been miraculously killed by the Sisters. This caused the Warboss to let go of Augusta, and she demanded to know how the Orks discovered the Sisters would be in the cathedral. The Warboss shrugged and simply explained that they were [[Blood Axes]] and the horde had come to take the Sisters' weapons for their own use. With that, Augusta knew her squadron had been betrayed and the likely suspect was Tanichus. The [[Missionary]] was the only one on [[Lautis]], that knew the Sisters were coming to search the cathedral. Augusta then ordered her squadron to find Tanichus, while Viola killed the Warboss when he grabbed a nearby [[grenade]]. Tanichus meanwhile had tried to escape, before he was captured by the Sisters and brought before Augusta.{{Fn|1}} 

Though he pleaded his innocence, Augusta pronounced Tanichus to be a [[heretic]] and told the missionary he should confess to save his soul. A terrified and sobbing Tanichus then admitted to his crimes and said the [[Orks]] had been destroying the world's villages, before he arrived. The [[Missionary]] was in a village near the cathedral, when the Orks approached it and in order to save the village's population, Tanichus made a deal with the [[Xenos]]. If the horde spared the village, he would bring the Sisters to the cathedral, where the Orks could then kill them and claim their weapons. But the Missionary swore he knew the Sisters would kill the Xenos and he was still loyal to the Imperium. With the truth now revealed, Augusta pronounced that Tanichus would die for his betrayal, which had cost the life of her Battle Sister [[Kimura]]. But she told the Missionary, that Lautis and its population would now be under the protection of the [[Order of the Bloody Rose]]. With that, Augusta executed the still pleading Tanichus, by slitting his throat with her Fleur-de-lys punch-dagger.{{Fn|1}}

===Lycheate===
While en route from [[Lautis]] to [[Ophelia VII]], Santorus and her squad under [[Melia Kaliyan]] receive new orders after detecting a distress symbol from one of [[Lycheate]]'s moons. There, they meet [[Inquisitor]] [[Istrix]] and [[Imperial Guard]] elements, who inform them that the moon has become a haven for [[Heretic]]s under former [[Interrogator]] [[Scafidis Zale]].{{Fn|3a}} The squad alongside Inquisitor Istrix and her retinue battles through heretics, questions arise as the Inquisitor seems to spare Zale, who is revealed to be her former disciple.{{Fn|3b}} Battling through a mob led by an [[Ork]] [[Freebooter]], the squad eventually tracks down Zale in the moon's manufactorum. A battle soon erupts when the squad opens fire on the Greenskin, despite Istrix insisting the Sisters hold their fire.{{Fn|3c}} In the ensuing battle against Zale's followers, it is revealed that Istrix has been psychically controlled by the heretic Interrogator the entire time. Imperial Guard [[Corporal]] [[Mors]] kills Istrix, while Zale launches a psychic assault upon Augusta and her sisters. In the end, Melia Kaliyan is able to kill Zale with her [[Flamer]].{{Fn|3d}}

Santorus and her squad next come into conflict with the [[Heretek]] [[Tech-Priest]] [[Rayos]], who also has been operating on [[Lycheate]]. Melia is demoted for having to killed an Inquisitor under suspicious circumstances, while Augusta is made squad commander.{{Fn|4a}} Moving on Rayos alongside reinforcements from the Order of the Bloody Rose, the Sisters move on the primary Heretek citadel under [[Canoness]] [[Elvorix Lanthe]]. Battling through [[Kastelan Robot]]s and [[Skitarii]] under Rayos' control in an assault led by [[Repressor]]s, [[Exorcist]]s, and [[Immolator]]s, the Sisters are eventually able to secure a manufactorum on the outskirts of the citadel and Canoness Lanthe suspects Rayos made be working with other Hereteks from [[Incaladion]].{{Fn|4b}} Augusta alongside Imperial Guard forces under Mors fight through a hidden tunnel entrance of the Citadel as the rest of the Sisters launch a frontal diversionary attack.{{Fn|4c}} 

Augusta's squad and the Guardsmen are able to reach the central forge-temple of the Citadel, where they encounter not just Rayos but also her master, [[Magos Dominus]] [[01-Vius]].{{Fn|4d}} In the ensuing battle, Melia is able to kill Rayos with her Flamer while Mors is slain by Vius. The Sisters are able to disable the [[Void Shield]] generators around the citadel, giving them only 90 seconds to flee before orbital bombardment begins. However Augusta stays behind to make sure Vius dies, eventually killing him with her [[Chainsword]]. The orbital bombardment destroys the citadel as Augusta and the rest of her squad narrowly escapes.{{Fn|4e}}

===Letum===
At some point, Augusta and her squad became stranded on [[Cemetery World]] of [[Letum (Cemetery World)|Letum]] and interacted with the mysterious and possibly heretical [[Order of the Broken Sepulchre]], much to their dismay. Upon investigating Letum, Augusta discovered that the world has a [[Xenos]]-derived magnetic field which forces ship to crash on its surface. Further investigations revealed that the Sisters had been sacrificing their young to the fierce storms around Letum for millennia, believing the maelstrom to be a manifestation of the [[Emperor]]'s power. However Augusta discovers that they are actually worshiping the slumbering beings beneath the surface, revealed to be [[Necron]]s. The Sisters above Letum's surface were apparently unaware of the true nature of their sacrifices. Augusta was able to destroy the central Necron obelisk at the center of the underground tomb complex, ending the storms and cycle of sacrifice. In the aftermath the [[Canoness]] of the Order vows to undertake a [[Crusade]] of penance which would begin by purging Letum of any further xenos taint.{{Fn|6a}}

===Opal===
Augusta and her squad were next dispatched to the world of [[Opal]] to retrieve the skull of [[Saint Veres]], which is a holy relic used every 800 years in a festival on the world. Upon arrival, they meet [[Deacon|Arch-Deacon]] [[Janos]] and [[Governor]] [[Vass Mihaly]], who are both reluctant to give up the skull, and the Sisters agree that the locals can use it temporarily for their festival while the Sororitas focus on quelling suspected dissidents on the world.{{Fn|5a}} Augusta's investigation leads her squad to the impoverished outskirts of Opal's primary [[Hive]]s, where they encounter a [[Genestealer Cult]] presence under the corrupted [[Priest]] [[Arkas]] and a hidden [[Genestealer Patriarch]].{{Fn|5b}} The Cult overwhelms the Sisters and initiates a general uprising on Opal's capital just as the festival begins.{{Fn|5c}} During the battle against the Genestealers, Melia is seemingly killed by Genestealer Cultists after confronting Arkas.{{Fn|5d}} 

Amidst the chaos of the fighting, a [[Tyranid]] fleet arrives in orbit alongside reinforcements led by Canoness Lanthe. The Sisters agree on a plan to exterminate Arkas and the Genestealer Patriarch while Opal is evacuated. Augusta's squad storm the outskirts citadel, killing the Patriarch as Deacon Janos is revealed to be a [[Genestealer Magus]] and is also slain by Sister [[Caia]].{{Fn|5e}} Augusta and her squad alongside the young cadet [[Kamilla]] are able to rescue Sister [[Akemi]] before killing Arkas, and they evacuate Opal with the rest of the Imperials.{{Fn|5f}} Afterwards in orbit aboard the ''Pride of Faith'' Augusta recommends Kamilla for the [[Schola Progenium]] to train as a fully-fledged [[Battle Sister]].{{Fn|5g}}

Aun Helwintr.wikitext:
{{SpaceWolvesPortal}}
'''Aun Helwintr''' was the senior [[Rune Priest]] of the [[Space Wolves]]' [[Space Marine Company|Tra Company]], during the [[Great Crusade]]{{Fn|1a}} and the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1b}}
==History==
As a new inductee into the [[Space Marine Company|Tra Company]], Helwintr took part in the campaign against the [[Olamic Quietude]], which saw the death of the senior [[Rune Priest]] [[Ulvurul Heoroth]]. In the aftermath of their successful battle, the Company's [[Wolf Lord]], [[Ogvai Ogvai Helmschrot]], selected Helwintr to replace Heoroth as Tra's senior Rune Priest.{{Fn|1a}} He also became the primary caretaker of the [[Skjald]] [[Kasper Hawser]] and later took part in the [[Council of Nikaea]] and the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Burning of Prospero]].{{Fn|1b}} 

During the battle on the [[Thousand Sons]]' [[Homeworld]], however, Helwintr sensed that terrible forces had been released in [[Prospero]]'s temple precinct. He sought to destroy it and gathered the [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]]s [[Patrekr]] and [[Cormek Dod]] to confront the threat, along with two dozen [[Silent Sisters]], who were led by [[Knight-Commander]] [[Jenetia Krole]]. The threat was soon revealed to be a [[Daemon]] shaped like the [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]], which had attacked and was about to kill the badly wounded Space Wolf [[Bjorn]] and the Skjald Hawser. Helwintr and the Dreadnoughts attacked the Daemon before it could do so, but the Daemon survived and was unharmed. It was only when Krole and her Sisters of Silence arrived, that their attacks began to have an impact. Thanks to the Sisters' [[Null]] abilities, the Daemon was soon overwhelmed by the Dreadnoughts' attacks and it was finally destroyed.{{Fn|1c}}

(Continues on as [[AI]] program){{Fn|3}} |Cause of Death =Killed by an [[Eversor Assassin]]{{Fn|3}} |Species ='' '' *[[Tau]] (Former) *[[A.I.]]{{Fn|3}} |Type = [[Aun]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation =[[Ethereal Supreme]] of the [[Tau Empire]] |Preceded by =[[Aun'Wei]] (As Ethereal Supreme) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Tau Empire]] **[[Ethereal Caste]] |Notes = }} '''Aun'Va''' is the most recent known [[T'au]] [[Ethereal Supreme]], the '''Aun'o''' of the [[T'au Empire]] and '''Master of the Undying Spirit'''.{{Fn|1a}} His full name was '''Aun'o'T'au'Acaya'Va'Denta''' and his title included Master of the Undying Spirit and stood as supreme Ethereal in the new [[Spheres of Expansion]] with [[T'au Commander|Commander]] [[Shadowsun]] at his side at all times. He led them forward to new frontiers and enemies.{{Fn|1a}} ===History=== Replacing the aging [[Aun'wei]], he was said to be the oldest of Ethereals and it was easy to see his effect on the expansion of the T'au Empire. He sat upon the highest councils governing not just [[Sept]]s but also the entire empire. Any advice he gave was always followed as his experience surpasses anything any other T'au has.{{Fn|1a}} It was said that none could deny his will, and that to even show disagreement with him seemed the most crass and boorish admission of ignorance.{{Fn|2a}} Although he was the spiritual leader of the T'au, he has also served on the very front lines in the early expansionist phase of the T'au Empire. He was instrumental in T'au planning during the [[Farsight Expedition]] and [[Great War of Confederation]]. His presence at the [[Si'coa system]] allowed the [[Fire Warrior]]s to destroy the [[Reek]] and upon the flanks of Mount Scion he described the fate of the [[Ork]] [[Waaagh! Grognik]], which the T'au swiftly followed, utterly destroying the Orks. During the [[Battle of Mu'gulath Bay]] during the [[Third Sphere of Expansion]], he personally accompanied [[Commander Shadowsun]] in the battle, which turned into one of the greatest Tau victories over the [[Imperium]].{{Fn|1a}} [[Image:AunvaDies.png|thumb|right|230px|The death of Aun'va and his entourage at the hands of a [[Culexus Assassin]] ]] During the [[Second Agrellan Campaign]], Aun'va became stranded on [[Mu'gulath Bay]] due to an Imperial blockade and took shelter in a hidden command bunker. However, his position was eventually discovered by the [[Officio Assassinorum]], which dispatched a [[Culexus Assassin]] to deal with him. The Culexus successfully infiltrated Aun'va's bunker, killing his bodyguards before pursuing and catching the Ethereal Supreme. Aun'va's end was neither swift or merciful. The [[Ethereal Council]] covered up his demise, using holograms of Aun'va to broadcast a victory speech after the loss of Mu'gulath Bay.{{Fn|3}} Few know of Aun'va's fate; instead, the Ethereal Supreme continues his duties as a hologram, with the original's personality and memories implanted into a AI-like device.{{Fn|4}} New edicts were declared to hide this deception, including forbidding any to touch Aun'Va and making sure his Honour Guards never leave him at any time.{{Fn|6}} This projection later appeared on [[Arthas Moloch]] to the embattled [[Commander Farsight]] in the [[Arks of Omen Campaign]]. Farsight had requested aid from the Tau Empire against common [[Ork]] and [[Chaos]] foes, but Aun'va informed the Commander that he was cursed for turning his back on the Greater Good and that all of his people were condemned with him.{{Fn|5}} ===Wargear=== *Aun'va was armed with the staff [[Paradox of Duality]]{{Fn|2b}} ===Images=== [[Image:AunVa2.jpg|center|thumb|Aun'Va on his hover chair with his [[Ethereal Guard|Honor Guard]]]] ===Sources=== *1: [[Codex: Tau Empire (6th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: pgs. 28-30 **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 60 *2: [[Codex: Tau Empire (7th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|2a}}: ''Ethereals - Ethereal Aun'Va'' **{{Endn|2b}}: pg. 80 - ''Aun'va - Master of the Undying Spirit'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[War Zone Damocles: Mont'ka]] - ''Spectre of Death'' *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Tau Empire (8th Edition)]], pgs. 33-36 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Arks of Omen: Farsight]], pg. 24-25 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Codex: T'au Empire (10th Edition)]], pg. 19 ===Uncited=== {{uncited}} *[http://uk.games-workshop.com/tau/gallery/17/ Tau miniatures gallery] {{TauForces}} [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[Category:Characters (T'au)]] [[Category:Characters (T'au Empire)]] [[de:Aun'Va]]

[[M41]] |Active Period =[[M41]] - Present |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Tau]] |Type =[[Aun]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation =[[Ethereal]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Tau Empire]] **[[Ethereal Caste]] |Notes = }} '''Aun’el Viora’la Shi''' is a [[T'au]] [[Ethereal]] from the [[Vior'la]] [[Sept]] of the [[T'au Empire]].{{Fn|3}} His titles include Master of the Blade, Saviour of the Fire Caste, Hero of [[Fio'vash (Town)|Fio'vash]], and The Aged Wonder.{{Fn|4}} A modest T'au hero of many battles who wields the [[Honour Stave]] ''[[Fidelity]]''{{Fn|5}}, Aun'shi longs for peace but is bound by duty to his comrades to wage war. Lionized by the [[Fire Caste]], he is seen as a good luck charm by those who have served with him.{{Fn|1b}} Aun'shi frequently accompanies [[Fire Warrior]] squads as '''Shas'aun'shi'''.{{Fn|1a}} Aun'shi is more comfortable in the company of [[Fire Warrior]]s. He may select any Fire Warrior team to act as his retinue. Such a team is clearly marked for glory.{{Fn|1b}} ===Biography=== [[Image:Aun'shi_Art.jpg|thumb|110px|right|Aun'shi]] In what was supposed to be his final assignment before retirement, he was sent to the planet of [[Kel'tyr]], to oversee a mining colony dealing with [[Feral Ork]] tribes.{{Fn|1b}} During the inspection of the town of [[Fio'vash (Town)|Fio'vash]], they came under attack by one such tribe of Orks, intent upon capturing the mine workings there. When the [[Shas'vre]] in charge of the Fire Warrior garrison was killed, Aun'shi dispatched a messenger and a [[Stealthsuit Team]] to the capital for help and in the meantime led the defence himself, slaughtering Orks by the dozen, armed with only his [[Honour Blade]].{{Fn|1b}} As dusk fell, Aun'shi and less than fifty Fire Warriors remained to protect the town. The T'au fell back to a barricaded shrine in the centre of the town, where they prepared to make their final stand. Aun'shi stood at the door to the shrine and stood his ground, not moving even when the doors themselves were ripped from their frames. Suddenly, the Ork forces were thrown into disarray as T'au reinforcements attacked: [[Devilfish]] troop carriers, [[Hammerhead Gunship]]s and [[Broadside Battlesuit]]s quickly devastating the Ork mobs and scattering the survivors. Aun'shi still stood at the shrine's door, his Honour Blade slick with Ork blood. The Ethereal shrine still stood and the mines of Fio'vash remained in Tau hands.{{Fn|1b}} His [[Defence of Fio'vash|defence]] of Fio'vash was considered a great victory, despite the horrendous casualties suffered by the T'au. When word reached the Ethereals on [[T'au (Planet)|T'au]], it was decreed that Aun'shi would continue to serve the [[Greater Good]] and further expand the [[T'au Empire]]. Aun'shi is considered to be a hero by the Fire Caste, and a huge marble bust of him was erected in the battledomes of [[Vior'la]].{{Fn|1b}} Aun'shi directed a major expedition to the [[Farsight Enclaves]] flagshipped by the ''[[Kessan|Dal'yth Gal'leath Kessan]]''.{{Fn|2}} ===Notes=== In the [[T'au Lexicon|T'au Language]] the ''shi'' in his name names ''Victory''.{{Fn|1c}} ===Images=== [[Image:Aun'shi.jpg|thumb|225px|center|Aun'shi miniature]] ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *1: [[Codex: Tau (3rd Edition)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: pg. 52 **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 53 **{{Endn|1c}}: pg. 57 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Battlefleet Gothic: Armada (Book)]], pg. 100 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Aun'Shi (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Tau Empire (6th Edition)]], pg. 64 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Codex: T'au Empire (9th Edition)]], pg. 104 ====Uncited==== {{Uncited}} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20080512024713/http://uk.games-workshop.com/tau/aunshi/1/ Master of the Blade AUN'SHI, HERO OF FIO'VASH] [[Games Workshop]] Website ''(saved archive page, dated June 2008)'' {{TauForces}} [[Category:Characters (T'au)]] [[Category:Characters (T'au Empire)]] [[de:Aun'shi]] [[fr:Aun'shi]]

'''Aun'ui Hoo'nan''' was a [[Tau Empire]] [[Ethereal]], that oversaw the hidden [[M'Yan'Ral]] [[Stormsurge]] facility on [[Sh'anshi]]{{Fn|1a}}. 

However it was later invaded by the [[Deathwatch]] and [[White Scars]] [[Chapter]], after its location was discovered by [[Watch Captain]] [[Nergui]]{{Fn|1b}}. The sudden attack, caught the facility's [[Fire Warriors]] off guard, though they quickly began to fight back against the invaders. This was not enough to stop the [[Imperium]]'s forces from invading deep within M'Yan'Ral, however, which caused its commander, the [[Fireblade]] [[M'au]], to fear for Hoo'nan's safety. This led the Fireblade to personally escort the Ethereal to a secured room, which he and several others Fire Warriors then guarded{{Fn|1c}}. However, the [[Watch Commander]] [[Jotunn]] had sensed their was an Ethereal in the facility and had begun a search for the Tau leader. He eventually found Hoo'nan's room and despite outnumbering the [[Space Marine]], M'au and his warriors were killed by Jotunn, who then killed the Ethereal as well.{{Fn|1d}}

'''Auramagma''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the 8th [[Chapter|Fellowship]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[Space Marine Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. Alongside [[Khalophis]] he too was a member of [[Cults of the Thousand Sons#Cult of the Pyrae|The Pyrae]]. Last seen apparently stricken unto death, he is presumed to have not survived the [[Burning of Prospero]],{{Fn|1}} although reports of a pyrokinetic once-Captain of the Legion called '''Malagor Auramagma''' existing on the [[Planet of Sorcerers]] after the days of the [[Horus Heresy]] confuse this issue somewhat.{{Fn|2}}

=== History ===
Auramagma was the Captain of the Thousand Sons' 8th Fellowship. He was a member of the Cult of Pyrae alongside fellow Captain Khalophis.{{Fn|1a}} Auramagma was regarded by more senior members of the Thousand Sons, such as [[Ahzek Ahriman]], as a reckless firebrand,{{Fn|1b}} and arrogant {{Fn|1d}}. Auramagma was noted to mockingly suggest that he and his fellow Captains attending The [[Council of Nikaea]] should remove one of their eyes as a symbol of solidarity with [[Magnus]].{{Fn|1c}}

He possessed significant psychic abilities that he was able to physically manifest liquid jets of fire which reportedly could melt [[ceramite]] as if it were wax. {{Fn|1e}} His full and unbridled power was unleashed on members of the [[Space Wolves]] Legion to great effect during their assault on the Thousand Sons home world.{{cite this}}

Auramagma is known to have directly confronted [[Leman_Russ_(Primarch)|Leman Russ]], the Space Wolves' Primarch during the fighting. Fellow Captain [[Phosis T'Kar]] witnessed Auramagma strike the Wolf King with wreath of psychic fire, engulfing him completely. For a brief moment, it was believed that this was a significant and potentially fatal blow to Russ. It appears that the chill armour worn by Russ reflected Auramagma's attack like a mirror and thus he himself was consumed in his own spell. ''"Auramagma howled in such agony that all who heard his screams were moved to pity as the aether devoured his very essence."''{{cite this}}

====Fate====
He was last seen, in what witnesses described as a blazing pyre of agony, fleeing the battlefield. The Space Wolves members parted before him, none apparently willing to go so near a damned soul. {{Fn|1e}}

Auramagma was not noted to be amongst the surviving members of the Thousand Sons Legion when they arrived on the [[Planet of Sorcerers]]. Despite the severe injury he received while duelling with Russ, his presumed demise is unconfirmed. His fate is further thrown into question by the appearance of a [[Chaos Champion]] of [[Tzeentch]] known as Malagor Auramagma, a pyrokine who once served as a Captain in the Thousand Sons legion and who is noted to have survived almost certain death on more than one occasion.{{Fn|2}}

===Notes===
Malagor Auramagma's appearance dates from 1st edition; considering the lack of first name used and his means of exiting the narrative, the more recent character of Auramagma from ''A Thousand Sons'' may simply be a nod to one of the few originally named pre-existing Thousand Sons rather than either a full retcon or an attempt to flesh the character out more. Regardless, it is interesting to note that in Malagor Auramagma's appearance he "once again had stared into the brink of death yet triumphed over it in the end."

'''Lady Aurelia Malys''', known as the '''Mazeweaver'''{{Fn|8}}, is a [[Dark Eldar]] [[Archon]] of the [[Kabal of the Poisoned Tongue]]. She leads her Kabal with a polite, if aloof and haughty manner that belies her great mind. Lady Malys, possessed of an incredibly byzantine mind, is highly intelligent to the point that she has matched [[Asdrubael Vect]] for wits time and again, and she is also amazingly precognitive and prone to elaborate treacheries and convoluted plots.  Her current position as one of the most successful Archons in [[Commoragh]] and her precognizant intellect may, in time, even overcome Vect himself.{{Fn|1a}}

===Biography===
In the time before her ascendancy, Malys had been a consort to Vect himself, and had been remarkably intelligent even then. In time Malys became one of the most prominent members of Vect's Inner Circle, particularly after the talent she displayed in the [[Panacea Wars]].{{Fn|1b}} After a time, Vect grew bored of the distraction Malys provided, and banished her from his court. Infuriated, Malys and her followers left Commoragh for the [[webway]]. In the "wilderness" of the webway, Malys had encountered one of the many strange beings that inhabit the realm. The being, rumoured to be [[Cegorach]] itself{{Fn|7}}, banished Malys' followers, and challenged her to a contest of wills, the victor of which would gain the heart of the loser. Amazingly, Malys had won the contest with the trickster, and the being had dissipated, leaving an animate blade and its crystal heart behind. Malys used the blade to remove her heart, and replaced it with her prize. The [[Harlequin]] Masque known as [[Masque of the Veiled Path|the Veiled Path]] is known to have indirectly arranged this meeting to create an arcane bond between Malys and [[Cegorach]]. Malys returned to Commoragh, determined to have revenge on Vect, and began her slow rise to power.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|3}}

In 345.[[M37]], Malys led her Kabal of the Poisoned Tongue against [[Ork]] [[Freebooterz]] on the world of [[Graegus]] after the Greenskin fleets raid her own forces. Malys captured a [[Nob]] and infected it with a deadly virus sensitive to the Ork reproduction cycle. Malys dropped her new biological weapon onto the Ork forces on Graegus many weeks later, annihilating the greenskin population.{{Fn|1c}}

In 999.[[M41]], Malys learns of Vect's capture of [[Null]]s in the [[Raid on Bakka (Dark Eldar)|Raid on Bakka]] as well as the instability of [[Khaine's Gate]]. Fearing that Vect plans to intentionally trigger its opening and drown his rivals in Daemons, the Archon of the Poisoned Tongue activates assets all across the Dark City. Waves of empyric energy roll from the Eye of Terror to batter Commorragh, collapsing sub-realms and breaching portals. Bands of [[Kabalite]]s, [[Wych]]es and [[Harlequin]]s loyal to Malys or Vect engage in increasingly bitter skirmishes around the Undercore, oblivious to the irony that both factions are fighting to achieve the same end. Meanwhile, in a chamber filled with swirling madness, hairline cracks spread across Khaine’s Gate.{{Fn|2}}

In early [[M42]], a series of massacres orchestrated by Vect were expertly evaded by Malys, who had seen the strikes coming and taken the entirety of the Poisoned Tongue to relatively unknown parts of the webway. Many of her rivals died during this time, allowing her to expand her influence remotely through her own agents or through puppet Kabals. She has come to completely control the Scarlet Harbour and Netherdell districts of Commorragh as well as numerous individual establishments. Outside of the city, Malys also has holdfasts hidden in the webway for the purposes of information gathering and the distillation of poisons, including one specialized toxin manufactory she established with a Grand [[Harlequin Masque]].{{Fn|5a}}

Using captured oracles, she divined the reappearance of a massive [[Space Hulk]] from the warp and that, should a particular Imperial ship be attacked beforehand, a mon-keigh prison barge containing a very valuable individual would come out of the warp close to the Hulk. The individual, an incredibly powerful [[psyker]], was not of value to her because of his abilities, but rather the fact that he was the bastard son of a human military commander, and only the commander, and those born of him, could open the weapon vaults on the planet [[Kesdimas]], which contain weapons capable of cracking entire continents. She planned to use the psyker to obtain those weapons, then use them against her rival, Archon [[Urethisk]] when she, encouraged by Malys, raids Kesdimas, and planned to blame Urethisk's death on the humans.{{Fn|5b}}
She sent one ship, containing multiple [[Hand of the Archon]] teams and a couple of escort ships, to the hulk to insert the teams in preparation for the prison barge's arrival, and employed [[Mandrake]] mercenaries to infiltrate the barge, called the ''[[Dyad of Zaffre]]'', itself. Once the ''Dyad'' was close enough to the Hulk, the Mandrakes emerged and opened webway portals, through which large numbers of her Poisoned Tongue emerged. They began slaughtering the crew and used [[Haywire Weapon|haywire]] charges that disabled several of the barge's important systems.{{Fn|5c}} Unfortunately, this caused the ''Dyad'' to collide with the Hulk, causing the instantaneous death of numerous of her servants.

Since the beginning of the [[Dark Eldar Civil War]], some have claimed Malys is building an alliance of Archons to finally remove Vect from power. Yet contradictory rumours persist that she is in fact Vect's agent and is instead drawing out potential enemies for him.{{Fn|8}}

===Combat===
Like most Dark Eldar Archons, Lady Malys is a swift and deadly opponent, and a ruthless and skilled leader.  Although intellectual and genteel, Malys is very dangerous in and of herself, and arms herself with a razor-edged steel fan and a sword called "[[Lady's Blade|The Lady's Blade]]".{{Fn|1a}} Presumably the same sword left behind after her contest in the webway, the sword is semi-sentient.{{Fn|1a}}

Both weapons are very deadly in her hands, though the Lady's Blade is prone to rebelling and crippling her combat capabilities. Due to her strange powers, she and her company are immune to [[psychic powers]] and she's precognizant enough to dodge weapons fire and enemy blows, or to stay one step ahead of her opponent's strategy.{{Fn|1a}}

[[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - ??? |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Ferrus Manus]] ("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Iron Father]] *[[Clan-Commander]] of the [[Morragul Clan]] (Former) *[[Chapter Master]] of the [[Red Talons]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Iron Hands]] ***[[Clan Morragul]] |Notes = }} '''Autek Mor''', known as the '''Maimed''' and the '''Blood-wrought''', was the [[Iron Father]] and Iron Lord of the [[Morragul Clan]] of the [[Iron Hands]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Horus Heresy]], and later became the first [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Red Talons]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|3}} ===History=== Mor had a sinister reputation within his own [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], and dark rumours maintained that the origins of his [[gene-seed]] were not as they should be. A [[Terra]]n by birth, he was one of the [[Iron Hands]]' first recruits and already a veteran before the rediscovery of [[Ferrus Manus]], taking part in the reconquest of the [[Sol System]]. By the time his [[Primarch]] was reunited with the ''X Legion'', he had already developed a reputation as both a weaponsmith and malevolent soul, having killed several of his own Legion in duels over slights to his honour and ruling his [[Clan Company]] with an iron fist.{{Fn|1}} On [[Medusa (Planet)|Medusa]] he took over the outlaw [[Ra'Guln]] Clan's [[Leviathan crawler]] in a bloody night of violence and made himself its lord, imprinting on it his name and will. In the years to follow, his [[Morragul Clan]] became a sinkhole for the outcasts and most unstable elements of the Legion. Mor and Ferrus Manus had no love for one another, but when his [[Grand Cruiser]] ''[[Red Talon]]'' arrived in the [[Isstvan System]], Mor nonetheless fought valiantly in a vain attempt to break though the traitor lines and extricate his [[Primarch]]. Mor's ship took heavy damage in the space battle and he fled the system, dogged by traitor pursuers.{{Fn|1}} Mor remained an active resistance fighter for the [[Loyalist]] cause following [[Drop Site Massacre|Isstvan]]. He rejected [[Shadrak Meduson]]'s strategy of waging guerrilla war against the traitors as an unworthy plan; instead, Mor would hurl his own forces directly at traitor-occupied worlds. Commanding a rag-tag [[Iron Hands]] strike force aboard the ''[[Red Talon]]'', Mor orchestrated a brutal campaign that targeted traitor recruitment and resource-producing centres. Notable examples of Mor's genocidal strategy included the nuclear [[Gethsamaine Raid|destruction]] of [[Gethsamaine Colonus]]' cities, the [[Battle of Bodt|razing]] of the [[World Eaters]]' primary mustering world of [[Bodt]] in 008.[[M31]] and the orbital scouring of the mining world [[Saria Major]]. To Mor, there were no innocent civilians in this conflict, only [[Loyalist]]s prepared to die for the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]] or those who aided the [[Horus|traitors']] cause in any fashion.{{Fn|2}} Following the [[Horus Heresy]], Autek Mor became the first [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Red Talons]], formed during the [[Second Founding]] from some of the most aggressive and volatile members of the [[Iron Hands]].{{Fn|3}} ===See also=== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] *[[List of Founders]] ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Two - Massacre]], pg. 237 *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Six - Retribution]], pg. 29 *{{Endn|3}}: [[The Vengeful Dead (Short Story)]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Mor, Autek}} [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Iron Hands)]] [[fr:Autek Mor]]

Skorr was considered by Alpharius to be a gifted diplomat, and was often used for missions that required a public face.{{Fn|3}} He had an honour to be mentioned in the [[Great Crusade]]'s [[War Council]] at least seven times for his outstanding performance in bringing to the compliance the newly discovered human worlds in the name of the [[Imperium]].{{Fn|2}} After the start of the [[Horus Heresy]] he actively participated in the [[Warmaster]]'s bloody "Dark Compliance" and at [[Epsilon-Stranivar IX]] [[the Shattered Legions]] were the only barrier between him and his victory.{{Fn|1}} Skorr treated his [[Iron Warriors]] allies poorly at both the [[Siege of Epsilon-Stranivar IX]] and the [[Siege of Mezoa]], using them as sacrificial pawns and cannon fodder. This caused [[Nârik Dreygur]] to defect to the [[Salamanders]] at the peak of the [[Mezoa]]n campaign, forcing Skorr into a hasty retreat. As he fled the world, he was badly wounded by [[Xiaphas Jurr]], losing an arm in the process.{{Fn|2}} ===Wargear=== Autilon Skorr is clad in the [[Artificer Armour]] with an embedded [[refractor field]] and he is armed with a [[bolt pistol]] and a [[Master-crafted]] [[power axe]].{{Fn|1}} ===Images=== [[Image:Autilon_Skorr.jpg|thumb|center|Autilon Skorr miniature{{Fn|1}}]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [https://www.forgeworld.co.uk/resources/fw_site/fw_pdfs/Horus_Heresy/Autilon.pdf Forge World 2015 Event-only model.] *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Six - Retribution]], pgs. 38–44,248 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Alpharius: Head of the Hydra (Novel)]] - ''Lord of the First'' {{DEFAULTSORT:Skorr, Autilon}} [[Category:Characters (Alpha Legion)]] [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[fr:Autilon Skorr]]
