'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a venerated member of the [[Blood Angels]], and the founder and [[Exalted Herald of Sanguinius|first commander]] of the [[Sanguinary Guard]], the Chapter's elite veteran fighting force and personal praetorians of the [[Primarch]] [[Sanguinius]]. Though his body is long since deceased, it has not decayed, something many hold to be an act of the [[Emperor]]'s grace. Moreover, many within the Sanguinary Guard suspect his soul to have become [[The Sanguinor]].{{Fn|1}}

===History===
====Pre-Heresy====
Azkaellon participated in the joint Blood Angels/[[Luna Wolves]] assault on [[Melchior]], fighting the [[Nephilim]]. Following the battle, it was discovered that Battle-brother [[Alotros]] of the [[111th Company (Blood Angels Legion)|111th Company]] had fallen to the [[Red Thirst]]. As one of the few who knew of the condition, Azkaellon helped [[First Captain]] [[Raldoron]] secure the site, but objected to Sanguinius becoming involved, saying that Alotros needed to be handled quietly. Sanguinius disagreed, saying that he needed to be there. While they saw Sanguinius go in, both Azkaellon and Raldoron were shocked to see both Sanguinius and [[Horus Lupercal]] emerge. Azkaellon rounded on Raldoron, saying his warriors were insufficient for the task at hand. Raldoron countered that his Sergeant [[Zuriel]] had equally failed to detect the Primarch of the Luna Wolves, and Azkaellon retorted that Zuriel would be disciplined for his failure, and Raldoron had little doubt of that.{{Fn|2a}}

Some years later, Azkaellon was dispatched with [[Task Force Ignis]] to locate a scientific colony on [[Nartaba Octus]], following rumours that there was a scientific facility that could help with dealing with the Red Thirst.{{Fn|2b}} However, the Blood Angels discovered that the planet was overrun with [[Dark Eldar]], who had destroyed the facility. Azkaellon would take little part in the battle of [[Nartaba Octus]] following this discovery,{{Fn|2c}} but did come to see [[Apothecary]] [[Meros]] when he learned that the battle-brother had been injured by a Dark Eldar soulseeker. Azkaellon had assumed that Meros would perish, but was impressed to discover that the Apothecary survived. He then relayed to Meros, Sergeant [[Cassiel (Blood Angels)|Cassiel]], and [[Sarga]] that the entire IX [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] was to rendezvous and converge on the [[Signus Cluster]], as per the orders of [[Warmaster]] Horus.{{Fn|3}} Before Task Force Ignis departed, however, a ship of the [[Space Wolves]] Legion carrying [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Helik Redknife]] and his squad arrived, carrying orders from [[Malcador (Character)|Malcador the Sigillite]] that the Wolves to observe. Azkaellon rebuked Redknife both for his reckless flying and the presence of [[Rune Priest]] [[Jonor Stiel]], saying that the [[Edict of Nikaea]] had forbidden [[Librarian]]s from using their powers. Redknife told Azkaellon that Stiel's power came from [[Fenris]], not the [[Warp]], and that was all the explanation they needed.{{Fn|2c}}

At some point during the Great Crusade, Azkaellon duelled [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] aboard an oceanic warship and, although Lucius won by drawing first blood, by this point Azkaellon had already tackled him over the side, humiliating him in front of his men and robbing Lucius of the perfect victory he wanted.{{Fn|7}}

====Heresy====
Azkaellon was present for the subsequent translation to the Signus Cluster, where a group of [[Word Bearers]] under [[Chaplain]] [[Tanus Kreed]] accompanied the Fleet. Azkaellon listened to strange background noise in [[vox]] transmissions, and dismissed it as merely a communications countermeasure.{{Fn|2d}} Upon reaching the bridge with his Primarch, he bore witness to the destruction of [[Phorus]]{{Fn|2e}} and subsequent meeting of the [[Council of Angels]], where Sanguinius ordered a scout team dispatched to [[Holst]] of Blood Angels and Word Bearers.{{Fn|2f}} However, the planet itself began attacking the Blood Angels, destroying the ''Paleknight''. Azkaellon then witnessed something he had never seen before: Sanguinius ordered Holst subjected to ''[[Exterminatus|exterminatus extremis]]'', destroying the whole of Holst. {{Fn|2g}} Azkaellon then debriefed the warriors who were present for the mission, along with First Captain Raldoron and [[Warden|High Warden]] [[Dahka Berus]], and was extremely skeptical of Apothecary Meros's tale.{{Fn|2h}} After the second mission to [[Scoltrum]] found survivors, Azkaellon was eager to know what they knew of the Nephilim, but Captain [[Dar Nakir]] said that they did not recognize them.{{Fn|2i}} As the Blood Angels fleet approached [[Signus Prime]], a psychic scream assailed the non-Astartes aboard the ship. Azkaellon was with Sanguinius and Raldoron when [[Kyriss]] the Perverse, the [[Keeper of Secrets]] who claimed rule of the Signus Cluster, greeted them.{{Fn|2j}}

Admiral [[Athene DuCade]], the [[Shipmaster]] of the ''[[Red Tear]]'', was driven mad and set the battleship on collision course with Signus Prime. Azkaellon advocated that they abandon ship, but Sanguinius refused, and the Blood Angels rode the ship down to the planet. Later, at a meeting of the Council of Angels, Meros told the assembled warriors that the ''[[Dark Page]]'', the vessel that carried the Word Bearers, had fled, leaving the ''Red Tear'' open, which Azkaellon confirmed. Captain [[Nassir Amit]] then revealed his concerns that Signus was a trap for the Angels, and that they had been betrayed by the Warmaster. Sanguinius nearly killed Amit in anger, but was stopped when Helik Redknife revealed that [[Magnus]] the Red, Primarch of the [[Thousand Sons]], had disobeyed the Edict of Nikaea. Azkaellon reacted by denying the revelations to himself, until Sanguinius ordered the Blood Angels to swear an [[oath of moment]] to eradicate the enemy.{{Fn|2k}}

Azkaellon accompanied Sanguinius in the subsequent [[Battle of Signus Prime]], but was separated from his Primarch when Sanguinius engaged [[Ka'Bandha]] the [[Bloodthirster]] and was injured.{{Fn|2l}} In his desperation to protect the Angel, Azkaellon shoved Meros aside as he tried to revive the Primarch, a wild look in his eyes. Teleporting back to the ''Red Tear'', the Apothecaries were unable to revive Sanguinius, and a malign influence began affecting the Blood Angels, inflaming their anger at the Primarch's injury. Unable to contact the rest of the Council of Angels, Azkaellon urged Raldoron to abandon the campaign to protect Sanguinius. [[Mkani Kano]], Raldoron's Adjutant and a former [[Librarian]], revealed that his brothers in the Librarium had gathered and were ready to use their powers to revive Sanguinius. Though Azkaellon opposed breaking the Edict, Raldoron agreed, leading a strike team including Meros and one of the survivors from Scoltrum, [[Tyllian Niobe]], who was a [[Pariah]], to destroy the Warpcraft causing the rage.{{Fn|2m}} Azkaellon remained with the Librarians, and warned that if he say any evidence of sorcery, he would cut their heads with his [[Glaive Encarmine]].{{Fn|2n}}

Despite his loyalty to Sanguinius, Azkaellon and the Sanguinary Guard gave into the rage and joined their brothers on the battlefield, abandoning the Primarch. Freed from the Warp's malign influence due to the sacrifice of Apothecary Meros, Azkaellon later helped oversee the removal of the Blood Angels presence in the Signus Cluster. When Warden Berus brought him the bodies of Helik Redknife and his fellow Space Wolves, they realized the importance of their wounds being caused by Space Marines, and kept the truth hidden from Sanguinius. Later, when Captain Amit confessed his role in the deaths of the Space Wolves to Raldoron, Azkaellon swore both warriors to silence, saying that if Sanguinius knew the truth, he would blame himself and would not lie to [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]], which threatened the solidarity of the Adeptus Asartes at a time of war. While Raldoron reluctantly saw the logic within, Amit asked how he would quiet the pain in his heart. Azkaellon told him that was his burden to bear.{{Fn|2o}}

Later in [[Imperium Secundus]]' capital of [[Macragge]], Azkaellon was guarding Sanguinius' throne room when he was set upon by [[Konrad Curze]] who had since been in hiding on the planet. Curze used the unconcious Azkaellon as a hostage so he could confide his own visions to Sanguinius. At the end of their talk, Curze cut off Azkaellon's arm and set off an explosive trap that mutilated the warrior before throwing him off a balcony. Choosing to rescue Azkaellon over pursuing Curze, Sanguinius caught the Sanguinary Guard. Azkaellon was badly wounded, but still alive.{{Fn|5}} Azkaelleon was later seen meeting with [[Drakus Gorod]] and [[Holguin]], who he had grown friendly with.{{Fn|6}}

During the journey through the [[Ruinstorm]] to try and reach Terra, Azkaellon continued to stand at Sanguinius' side. Azkaellon fought alongside Sanguinius both at [[Battle of Pyrrhan|Pyrrhan]] and [[Second Battle of Davin|Davin]], and in the latter desperately sought to rescue his Primarch from the clutches of [[Madail]].{{Fn|8}} During the [[Battle of Beta-Garmon]] Azkaellon led a boarding action against a traitor-occupied [[Starfort]] ''The Anvil'', capturing it but narrowly escaping before it detonated after realizing it was a trap.{{Fn|9}}

During the [[Battle of Terra]], Azkaellon was constantly worried by Sanguinius' attempts to journey outside the safety of the [[Sanctum Imperialis]] in order to inspire Imperial troops. During the traitor assault on the Helios Gate of the Palace, Azkaellon and his Sanguinary Guard charged into hordes of [[Death Guard]], [[World Eaters]], and [[Night Lords]] alongside their Primarch.{{Fn|10}} Sanguinius would later order Azkaellon to remain in the [[Imperial Palace]] when he joined the Emperor and [[Rogal Dorn]] in boarding the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'' to face Warmaster Horus. After the fall of [[Bhab Bastion]], Azkaellon rallied with remaining loyalist officers such as [[Fafnir Rann]], [[Namahi]], [[Dominion Zephon|Zephon]], [[Maximus Thane]], [[Satel Aimery]] in the final defense of the Inner Palace under the command of [[Archamus II|Archamus]].{{Fn|11}}

However upon sensing the death of their Primarch at the hands of Horus, the Blood Angels erupted into fury as the [[Black Rage]] took hold. Azkaellon was amongst those who succumbed to the madness, and became little more than a feral beast that slaughtered loyalist and traitor alike. Soon enough he even attacked his friend Fafnir Rann, who at first was reluctant to strike down his brother but soon found he couldn't even if he wanted to. The fight was only interrupted due to attacks by World Eaters and Death Guard, whom Azkaellon feasted upon.{{Fn|12a}} After the defeat of Horus and the lifting of the madness, Azkaellon took part in a funeral service for Sanguinius alongside Raldoron and perhaps 500 other surviving Blood Angels.{{Fn|12b}}

====Post-Heresy====
With the rest of the Sanguinary Guard lost aboard the ''Vengeful Spirit'', Azkaellon was the sole survivor of his order. Azkaellon would later oversee the division of the Blood Angels Legion into numerous [[Chapter]]s{{Fn|1}} alongside Raldoron, who would become the first Chapter Master of the Blood Angels.{{Fn|4}}

===Personality===
Azkaellon was extremely loyal to Sanguinius, to a degree that disturbed First Captain Raldoron. When Raldoron asked if Azkaellon would truly abandon his own battle-brothers, Azkaellon told the First Captain to his face that he would willingly sacrifice any warrior of the IX Legion for the Primarch's protection.{{Fn|2m}} Azkaellon was also extremely rigid in his manner. Where as Raldoron was fluid and adaptable in combat, Azkaellon was unyielding, another cause of friction between the Sanguinary Guard and the First Company.{{Fn|2a}}

===Wargear===
Like the rest of the Sanguinary Guard, Azkaellon wore a golden suit of [[Artificer Armour]] and a [[Winged Jump Pack]], and wielded a Glaive Encarmine for close combat and an [[Angelus-pattern boltgun]] on his left wrist.{{Fn|2a}}

===Conflicting sources===
The original lore of the Blood Angels stated that Azkaellon was the sole Sanguinary Guard to survive the Heresy, but  [[The End and the Death: Volume III (Novel)|The End and the Death]] novels present another, [[Taerwelt Ikasati]], as surviving.{{Fn|12b}}

Baertrum Arturos III.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
[[file:Arturos.jpg|thumb|right|200px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]

'''Baertrum Arturos III''' is a [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]n '''[[Adjurators|Adjurator]]''', which are the [[Hive Primus]] [[Merchant Guild]]s' own private order of [[bounty hunter]]s.{{Fn|1}}

Adjurators are hired when a Guilder is concerned with the recovery of their own property and the reprimand of those responsible for taking it. However after one such bounty took Arturos into the [[Underhive]], to run down a [[clan tithe-breaker]], he developed a taste for that fringe realm and chose to remain there. Although he could easily make more scrip in the mid-[[Hive]] domes, Arturos likes the way the Underhive's population look at him with a mixture of fear and disgust, while the filthy environment reminds him that he was born of higher stock. Plus in the Underhive, the Adjurator can throw his authority around, more easily than he could in the upper Hive levels. Despite his dislike of the Underhive's population though, Arturos is not above allying himself with them, when his interests and theirs co-align. This leads him to often works with [[gang]]s, who hire the Adjurator because he is always cool-headed, quick with his [[Needle Pistol]] and shrewd enough to avoid being ambushed. They do have to put up with Arturos' frequent scowls, condescending sneers and long diatribes in return, but it is a small price to pay for the Adjurator's talents and the veneer of Guild authority he brings with him.{{Fn|1}}

He was the "winged phoenix" and taught the [[Swooping Hawk]] [[Aspect]].{{Fn|2}} He is also the brother of [[Maugan Ra]], like the sun is to the moon, and many of the Eldar's foes have been killed on the edge of their blades.{{Fn|3}} ===History=== The creator of the Aspect Shrine of Swooping Hawks, he is the youngest Phoenix Lord who fought side by side with Maugan-Ra in their early days after the [[Fall of the Eldar|Fall]] under the tutelage of [[Asurmen]].{{Fn|4}} He was the first of the Phoenlix Lords to master aerial combat.{{Fn|8}} Known to move with both elegance and the force of a hurricane, Baharroth epitomizes speed and grace.{{Fn|2}} According to the [[Asuryata]], Baharroth's final death will come at the dawning of the [[Rhana Dandra]].{{Fn|8}} He has, like all other Phoenix Lords, has died and been reincarnated several times, and it is said he will meet his fate at the [[Rhana Dandra]], the final battle against Chaos.{{Fn|3}} He wields the [[Shining Blade]], a weapon forged by the daughters of [[Vaul]] in the dying flames of a supernova{{Fn|4}} as well as the [[Lasblaster]] ''[[Fury of the Tempest]]''.{{Fn|6}} Baharroth later appeared under the command of [[Jain Zar]], now pledged to [[Ynnead]]. Baharroth took part in the battle to defend the [[Ynnari]] against the [[Thousand Sons]] and [[Tzeentch]] [[Daemon]]s in the [[Webway]], vanishing during the struggle.{{Fn|5}} ===Images=== Baharroth.jpg|Miniature (2nd Edition){{Fn|1}} Baharroth10th.jpg|Miniature (10th Edition){{Fn|7}} Baharroth by John Gravato.JPG|Baharroth The Cry of the Wind ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/en-US/Phoenix-Lord-Baharroth Games Workshop] ''(last accessed 7 May 2015)'' *{{Endn|2}}: [[Codex: Eldar (6th Edition)]] (E-Book), pg.97 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Eldar (6th Edition)]], pg. 60 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Craftworlds (7th Edition)]] (e-book), ''Baharroth - Remnants of Glory'' *{{Endn|5}}: [[Gathering Storm: Fracture of Biel-Tan]] *{{Endn|6}}: [[Codex: Aeldari (9th Edition)]], pg. 150 - Datasheets *{{Endn|7}}: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241123030033/https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-us/articles/gw3wcpc7/world-championships-preview-aeldari-phoenix-lords-step-from-the-webway/ Warhammer Community: World Championships Preview – Aeldari Phoenix Lords step from the webway (posted 22/11/2024)] ''(saved archive page, dated 23 November 2024, last accessed 24 November 2024, original link: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-us/articles/gw3wcpc7/world-championships-preview-aeldari-phoenix-lords-step-from-the-webway/ here])'' *{{Endn|8}}: [[Codex: Aeldari (10th Edition)]], pg. 41 {{EldarUnits}} [[Category:Characters (Craftworld Eldar)]] [[Category:Phoenix Lords]] [[de:Baharroth]]

Baldo Umbaldi.wikitext:
[[File:Baldo Umbaldi.jpg|thumb|Baldo Umbaldi{{Fn|1b}}]]'''Baldo Umbaldi''' is a [[traitor]] warlord, who claims to rule the deserts of an unknown [[hive world]].{{Fn|1a}} ==History== Once a warlord (perhaps leading hive gangs) in one of the planet's hives, he was cast out and left to die in the hostile desert wastes, possibly for [[Chaos|Chaotic]] allegiance or [[Psyker|psychic powers]]. Thought to be long since forgotten by his former hive's inhabitants, he survived, becoming far stronger and more powerful, eventually emerging as the leader of thousands of loyal warriors, each willing to die for him. Viciously guarding his territory from trespassers, he waits for an impending [[Tyranid]] invasion, which he plans to defeat and return to the hive as its saviour.{{Fn|1a}} ==Warning== {{QuoteBox|width=30em|title=Let it be known!|qalign=center|quote=I, Baldo Umbaldi do declare that all who pass beyond this sign are doomed to die a slow and agonising death, torn limb from limb and left to rot in the flaming pits of Chaos for all eternity, for the crime of trespassing upon my sacred territory.
:...
Only I have the power to give life in this forsaken place. Return from whence you came. Go back to your accursed hive. Tell all you see about me, Baldo Umbaldi, for one day I shall return. As sure as the sun rises each day, when this world grows old and the [[Great Devourer]] comes, I shall return, to be your salvation.
So turn back now, weary traveller, for your journey is not yet done.}}Umbaldi left a sign to warn travellers from the hive not to enter his domain on pain of torture and death, and stating his history and planned return. Apparently illiterate, Umbaldi signed it with a X mark by his name.{{Fn|1a}} ==Power== It is unclear if Umbaldi has psychic powers, is aligned to Chaos or simply claims great power. As well as temporal control of the desert and sole possession of the power to give life there, he claims to be able to kill unwanted travellers by a number of excruciating methods:{{Fn|1a}} *Tearing limb from limb and burning in the pits of Chaos *Setting on fire and burning all flesh *Infestation with pustulent boils and stomach eating maggots *Death by the lashing, choking and corroding effect of the wastes' acidic sand storms ==Equipment== Baldo Umbaldi uses a [[slug-thrower]] gun (similar in design to a small [[heavy stubber]]), and a [[chainsword]] (with "An eye for an eye" written along the length of the blade). He wears a spiked helmet and a large fur coat, carrying a large [[respirator]] on his back to allow him to survive the harsh environment of the wastes. Having lost his right leg, he uses an ornate replacement peg-leg.{{Fn|1a}} ==Sources== *1: [[Inferno! 2]] **{{Endn|1a}}: pgs. 44-45 - ''Baldo Umbaldi'' **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 3 {{DEFAULTSORT:Umbaldi, Baldo}} [[Category:Characters (Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Renegades)]]

Baldr Fjolnir.wikitext:
{{SpaceWolvesPortal}}
{{ambig|subject=Grey Hunter|disambiguation=Baldr}}
'''Baldr Fjolnir''' was a [[Grey Hunter]] of the [[Space Wolves]] [[Chapter]]{{Fn|1a}}, serving in the [[Blackmanes]] [[Great Company]] as a member of [[Járnhamar Pack]].{{Fn|1b}}

==History==
Baldr accompanied his Pack under [[Gunnlaugur]] to [[Ras Shakeh]], during which he became infected by a [[Nurgle]] plague.{{Fn|1c}} Falling into a coma, Baldr is guarded over by [[Ingvar]] as the city of Hjec Aleja is besieged by [[Chaos]] forces.{{Fn|1d}} At the height of the battle, he reawakens and saves his Pack from the [[Chaos Space Marine]] champion [[Thorslax the Blighted]] with sudden [[Psyker|psychic]] abilities before falling back into a coma.{{Fn|1e}}

Eventually awakening in the presence of [[Njal Stormcaller]], Baldr is cleared of any overt taint but the [[Rune Priest]] remains suspicious.{{Fn|2a}} Along with Njal and the bulk of his Pack, he takes part in the assault of the Nurgle [[Space Hulk]] ''[[Festerax]]'', during which Baldr is captured by the [[Sorcerer]] [[Mycelite]]. Mycelite plans to use Baldr's psychic abilities to fuse his psyche with that of the Hulk, giving him full control over the ancient vessel revealed to be [[Space Wolves]] in origin.{{Fn|2b}} He is enslaved by Mycelite and forced to battle Njal, but the Rune Priest is able to break his psychic-dampening null-collar. In the sudden burst of power, Baldr kills Mycelite and regains control of himself.{{Fn|2c}} In the aftermath of the massive display of power, Baldr is judged a [[Psyker|witch]] by Njal and condemned to execution. This does not sit well with the rest of Járnhamar Pack, which rescue him and flee their own Chapter as renegades.{{Fn|2d}}

Seeking a mysterious individual known as "Fulcrum" for a chance of redemption, Baldr's psychic guidance proves key in the endeavor.{{Fn|3a}} They eventually pursue clues to [[Ojada VII]], finding that the Fulcrum is the heretical [[Cardinal]] [[Leon ­Chirastes]].{{Fn|3b}} This leads them to Chirastes conspiracy to assassinate [[Ragnar Blackmane]], who Baldr insists is not on [[Fenris]]. At the same time, Baldr's vision includes visions of [[Battle of the Fenris System|Fenris' devastation]].{{Fn|3c}}

Thanks to Baldr's psychic guidance, the pack is eventually able to find Ragnar on [[Cadia]], waging the [[13th Black Crusade]].{{Fn|3d}} hey eventually travel to [[Kasr]] Vasta, coming across the dying [[Eldar]] [[Warlock]] [[Caerlainn]]. She removes Baldr's null-collar in exchange for the Space Wolf taking her [[Spirit Stone]] and return it to her people. With Baldr's psychic nullification gone, he is able to detect Ragnar's precise location in Kasr Vasta and reaches his full pinnacle as a Psyker.{{Fn|3e}} However just before reaching Ragnar, Baldr is overcome by another psychic revelation of the fall of Cadia and realizes he has another mission to attend to. Baldr descends into the tunnels deep beneath Kasr Vasta as the rest of Járnhamar Pack completes their mission, and goes missing after.{{Fn|3f}}

'''Bale Rane''' was an [[Imperial Army]] trooper, who served in [[Calth]]'s [[Numinus 61st]] [[Regiment]], during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

===Biography===
He was a teenager, when his [[Regiment]] was preparing to take part in the [[Ghaslakh Crusade]], which would force Bale to leave his new wife, [[Neve Rane|Neve]], behind.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}} However before the [[Crusade]] launched from [[Calth]], the [[Word Bearers]] [[Battle for Calth|attacked]] the world as the [[Horus Heresy]] began. As the invasion raged, Bale soon joined a small group of [[Imperials]] who escaped with the [[Perpetual]] [[Ollanius Persson]] into a [[Warp Rift]] he created. This began a journey through time and space, as Persson tried to reach [[Terra]] before the traitorous [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] could kill the [[Emperor]]. Even as the group was then faced with countless dangers, however{{Fn|2a}}, Bale's thoughts always dwelt on his wife, whom he had been unable to rescue before the group escaped from Calth.{{Fn|2b}} 

When the group arrived on [[Terra]], they found themselves in a horrific dream-garden of the [[Emperor's Children]] known as Paradise. Within the realm, Rane saw visions of his wife beckoning to him and was overcome by a desire to be reunited with her. However this was a trap, and Rane was killed by [[Daemon]]s.{{Fn|2c}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Captain]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

===History===
Leading the [[Fifth Fellowship]], he commanded the [[Athanaean]] Cult, the telepathy specialists of the [[Legion]]. A native of [[Prospero]], Uthizzar took command of the 5th Fellowship after the previous captain [[Apophis]] was killed in battle against [[Orks]].{{Fn|1a}} Uthizzar later briefly battled the [[Space Wolves]] during the [[Ark Reach Secundus]] incident where many of his Athanaeans were killed by the psychic backlash caused by [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]].{{Fn|1b}}

Later after his failed attempt to warn the [[Emperor]], [[Magnus]] fell into a depression. He was confronted by Uthizzar who was accidentally exposed to the [[Primarch]]'s psychic power. In an instant, Uthizzar saw much of Magnus' past including his secret dealings with [[Tzeentch]] in an attempt to rid the Thousand Sons of their Flesh Change mutation. Horrified by what he had seen, Baleq attempted to leave to inform the rest of his Legion but was killed by a psychic blast by Magnus.{{Fn|1c}} As  Prospero was [[Burning of Prospero|invaded and destroyed]] by the Imperial Censure Host soon after, it is unclear who immediately succeeded Uthizzar in commanding the Fifth Fellowship; however, a lone officer named [[Sul Kontep]] ultimately took charge of the Fellowship amid the ruins of Prospero.{{Fn|2}}

===Notes===
Not to be confused with [[Uzthizarr]], a character who only differs from Baleq Uthizzar in the slightly different spelling of their name, and that Uzthizarr survives the Battle of Prospero and becomes a [[Daemon Prince]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Chief Librarian]] of the [[Raven Guard]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]{{fn|1a}} before becoming one of [[Malcador (Character)|Malcador the Sigillite]]'s [[Knights-Errant]].{{fn|2}}


===Biography===
Balsar Kurthuri was a [[Librarian]] in the [[Raven Guard]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]] until the [[Edict of Nikaea]]; he was then forced to become a [[Legionary]]. He would later take part in the [[Horus Heresy]] and was one of the few of his Legion to survive the [[Dropsite Massacre]]. Afterwards, Balsar was chosen to become his depleted Legion's [[Chief Librarian]] when his [[Primarch]] [[Corax]] reinstated the Raven Guard's [[Librarius (Fortress-monastery)|Librarius]].{{fn|1a}}

In the later years of the Horus Heresy, Balsar's standing within the Legion would change once more, after a meeting with his fellow Librarian [[Fara Tek]]. Fara had just rendezvoused with his Legion, where it was gathering in the [[Rosario System]], and shared with Balsar a psychic message he had received before he had rejoined them. Though the message was not clear, Balsar gathered from it that the Primarch [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]]' life was in danger, but little else. He could not tell Balsar where the message had come from, though he had been able to receive another message from a nearby [[Space Wolves]] [[Strike Cruiser]]; that was being attacked by the [[Word Bearers]] and needed aid. Balsar immediately brought this information to Corax, who dispatched [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Agapito Nev]], and the [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Providence (Battle Barge)|Providence]]'', to save the Space Wolves Strike Cruiser. Agapito succeeded in doing so and brought the Strike Cruiser's commander, [[Rathvin]], to meet with Corax. The Space Wolf proceeded to inform the Raven Guard's Primarch, that Leman Russ was indeed in danger, as his Legion had been cornered on the world [[Yarant Three]] by Horus' forces, which heavily outnumbered them.{{fn|1a}}

Rathvin would leave shortly afterwards, to join his his Legion in battle, and Corax quickly gathered his commanders and informed them the Raven Guard were going to Yarant Three to aid the Space Wolves. Balsar was shocked however, when his Primarch informed him that he would not be joining them and that he had also been stripped of his title of Chief Librarian; as Corax had once again disbanded the Raven Guard's Librarius. For reasons unknown to Balsar, Corax had grown deeply mistrustful of [[psyker]]s and wanted his former Librarians to be immediately separated from his Legion and sent away to [[Terra]]. Though Balsar was eventually able to convince his Primarch, to let his fellow psychic brethren remain with the Legion, as long as they did not use their powers, the former Chief Librarian's fate was sealed. Corax commanded him to depart for Terra at once and told Balsar that when he arrived there, he was to present himself to [[Malcador the Sigillite]], who would decide what would become of him.{{Fn|1b}}

When Kurthuri arrived in the [[Sol System]], accompanied by Captain [[Noriz]] and his [[Imperial Fists]] and [[Arcatus]] and his [[Legio Custodes|Custodians]], the Custodian [[Ludivicus]] gave the order to hunt the Librarian down. Arcatus immediately obeyed, attacking Kurthuri on the bridge, but Noriz attempted to help him escape the ship. Cornered by Arcatus, Noriz was killed by the Custodian, but Kurthuri was spared when he backed down from using his psychic powers to avenge the captain's death. Kurthuri was brought before Malcador the Sigillite and presented with a suit of grey [[power armour]] by [[Umojen]], becoming one of the [[Knights-Errant]].{{Fn|2}}

It is possible that Balsar Kurthuri became [[Ogen]], one of the founders of the [[Grey Knights]].

Baltan.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Baltan''' was a [[Commissar]] assigned to a [[Armageddon Steel Legion]] force, sent to the [[Hive World]] [[Sephlagm]], to put down a [[Chaos Cult]] rebellion.  Unfortunately for the Legion, the [[Dark Angels]] were also on Sephlagm hunting for a [[Fallen Angel]] who they believed to be on the Hive World.  As the Steel Legion traveled to a Cultist hotspot, they were attacked by the Dark Angels, who began cracking open their vehicles in search of the Fallen Angel, exposing their crews to the Hive World's deadly atmosphere.  Seeing the Steel Legion being undone vehicle by vehicle, Baltan gave the order for the Legion to fire upon the traitorous Dark Angels.  It did no good, however, as the weakened Legion were no match for the Dark Angels and were easily beaten.  Before they could be finished off, however, the surviving Dark Angels suddenly teleported away - just before a [[Deathstrike Missile Launcher|Deathstrike missile]] struck the battlefield, killing Baltan and destroying the Steel Legion force.{{Fn|1}}

(as Master of the 5th Company){{Fn|8}} |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Dark Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Balthasar''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Company Master]] of the [[Dark Angels]] [[5th Company (Dark Angels)|Fifth Company]].{{Fn|1}} Balthasar was promoted from his post as a [[Deathwing]] [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] to succeed Company Master [[Zadakiel]], who died at the hands of the [[Crimson Slaughter]] [[Chaos Warband|Warband]]. His lifetime of servitude to the Deathwing honed Balthasar into a crafty and cunning tactician. He held a great personal anger against the Crimson Slaughter for murdering his mentor.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|5}} Balthasar was known amongst the [[Inner Circle]] of the [[Chapter]] for his low tolerance of [[psyker]]s, although his negative opinions of the Dark Angels' own [[Librarian]]s were more due to his conviction that their psychic powers were the reason why they were chosen to become [[Space Marines]], rather than skill in battle.{{Fn|3a}}{{Fn|3b}} ==Biography== ===Early History=== [[Image:Balthasar.jpg|thumb|right|135px|Company Master Balthasar{{Fn|2}}]] Balthasar grew up on one of the thousands of worlds that the Dark Angels swore an oath to protect and, in turn, draw [[aspirant]]s from. That world had labored under the oppression of a [[Psyker|psychic]] [[cult]] until it was brought down by a resistance movement, of which Balthasar was a member. This is what led to Balthasar's distrust towards psykers.{{Fn|3c}} ===Battle for Honoria=== *{{Main|Battle for Honoria}} {{Spoiler|source=Eye of Ezekiel (Novel)}} In 949.M14{{Fn|9}}, when Balthasar was a [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] of the Fifth Company, he took part in the [[Battle for Honoria]].{{Fn|3b}} During the mission, [[Ezekiel]] was tasked by [[Chief Librarian|Grand Master]] [[Danatheum]] to assess whether Balthasar should ascend to the [[Deathwing]] (a replacement was needed following the death of [[Joadar]]).{{Fn|3a}} During the defence of [[Honoria (Planet)|Honoria's]] capital city, [[Aurelianum]], [[Space Marine Captain|Company Master]] [[Zadakiel]] was wounded by the [[Ork]] [[Warboss]] [[Groblonik]]. Although he survived, he had to enter a [[Sus-an Membrane|sus-anic healing coma]]; Balthasar assumed acting control of the Fifth Company for the remainder of the Dark Angels' time on Honoria.{{Fn|3d}}{{Fn|3e}} Although Ezekiel decided that Balthasar was worthy of a position in the Deathwing, impressed by his actions on Honoria, the Librarian thought Balthasar was not yet ready for the position.{{Fn|3f}} Eventually, however, Balthasar did earn a place in the Deathwing.{{Fn|4c}} ===Pandorax Campaign=== *{{Main|Pandorax Campaign}} {{Spoiler|source=Pandorax (Novel)}} In 960.[[M41]] Balthasar, now a member of the [[Deathwing]], fought in the [[Pandorax Campaign]]. He took part in the battle on the [[asteroid]] [[Malefus Murex]] when the Chapter initially arrived in system, then [[teleport]]ed over to the ship ''[[Revenge]]'' with the rest of First Company to help the [[Grey Knights]] capture it. He still held his bias against [[psykers]], despite working with Ezekiel on Honoria, and called psykers "witchminds" directly to [[Kaldor Draigo]].{{Fn|10}} ===Deathwatch=== {{Spoiler|source=Deathwatch: The Last Guardian (Audio Drama)}} While a member of the Deathwing, Balthasar was seconded to the [[Deathwatch]] for a period of 12 years.{{Fn|4c}} He was part of a [[Kill-Team]] sent by an [[Inquisitor]] to investigate the remains of the destroyed [[Eldar]] [[Craftworld]] known as [[Kher-Ys]]. Within the Craftworld's [[Infinity Circuit]], they found the [[Ruin of Kher-Ys]] - the [[Spirit Stone]] of the Eldar whose actions allowed the [[Daemon]] [[Heartslayer]] to manifest on the Craftworld.{{Fn|4a}} Balthasar and his [[Watch Captain]] were the only two members of the Kill-Team alive by this point, the Watch Captain intending to turn the spirit stone over to the [[Ordo Xenos]]. However, Balthasar and the Inquisitor killed the Captain, revealing that the mission was to secure the stone for the Dark Angels. The Inquisitor died shortly afterwards, succumbing to the wounds she sustained when she was stabbed by a [[Keeper of Secrets]]. With her last words, she asked Balthasar to tell [[Azrael]] that her debt to them was paid.{{Fn|4b}} Upon returning to [[The Rock]], Balthasar was questioned about the mission by [[Interrogator-Chaplain]] [[Asmodai]]. His superiors were satisfied by his work in the Deathwatch and Balthasar returned to the ranks of the Deathwing with none of his battle-brothers learning of his mission.{{Fn|4c}} ===Stern's Rememberance=== In 578999.[[M41]]{{Fn|7c}} Balthasar was part of a Deathwing squadron attached to the Fifth Company, at the time still under the command of Master Zadakiel, that travelled to the planet [[Stern's Rememberance]] to hunt the [[Fallen Angel]] [[Attias|Attias the Untamed]]. However, Attias was merely bait for an ambush; the Dark Angels were attacked by the [[Crimson Slaughter]]. In the ensuing conflict, Zadakiel was killed and Balthasar became Company Master of the Fifth in his place.{{Fn|5}}{{Fn|7a}} ===5th Company Captain=== *{{Main|Battle for Bane's Landing}} In 884999.[[M41]]{{Fn|7c}} He eventually defeated [[Sevastus Kranon|Kranon the Relentless]] and his Chaos Space Marine Warband in the [[Battle for Bane's Landing]], with help from Librarian [[Turmiel]] and other forces of the [[Dark Angels]] Fifth Company.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|6}}{{Fn|7b}} Balthasar would later be killed in the chaotic battles that followed the [[Great Rift|Great Rift's]] creation and was succeeded by Master [[Lazarus (Dark Angels)|Lazarus]].{{Fn|8}} ==See also== *[[List of Space Marine Captains]] ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[White Dwarf 392]], pg. 35 *{{Endn|2}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/gws/catalog/productDetail.jsp?catId=&prodId=prod1700019a Games Workshop] *3: [[The Eye of Ezekiel (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter One **{{Endn|3b}}: Chapter Three **{{Endn|3c}}: Chapter Five **{{Endn|3d}}: Chapter Twelve **{{Endn|3e}}: Chapter Thirteen **{{Endn|3f}}: Epilogue *4: [[Deathwatch: The Last Guardian (Audio Drama)]]: **{{Endn|4a}}: Track 12 **{{Endn|4b}}: Track 13 **{{Endn|4c}}: Track 14 *{{Endn|5}}: [[The Ascension of Balthasar (Audio Drama)]] *{{Endn|6}}: [[Dark Vengeance (Novella)]] *7: [[Crimson Slaughter - A Codex: Chaos Space Marines Supplement (6th Edition)]]: **{{Endn|7a}}: pg. 25 - ''Dark Vengeance'' **{{Endn|7b}}: pg. 26 - ''Battle of Bane's Landing'' **{{Endn|7c}}: pg. 35 *{{Endn|8}}: [[White Dwarf September 2019]], pg. 28 - ''Index Astartes: Dark Angels'' *{{Endn|9}}: [[Codex: Dark Angels (6th Edition)]], pg. 25 *{{Endn|10}}: [[Pandorax (Novel)]], Chapter 9 [[Category:Characters (Dark Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Deathwatch)]] [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]]

Baltus.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Tactical Squad|Tactical Marine]] of the [[Dark Angels]]' [[4th Company (Dark Angels)|4th Company]], who was part of his [[Chapter]]'s strike force sent to secure the [[Calaphrax Cluster]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
[[Image:Baltus.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Brother Baltus]]
{{PAGENAME}} served under [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Kalidius]] when the Company was sent to secure the [[Calaphrax Cluster]] in [[M41]]. His squad was the first deployed to the surface of [[Exyrion]] to investigate the [[Dead World]].{{fn|1a}} They discovered an underground [[hive]] was home to a number of survivors,{{fn|1b}} drawing power from the [[Orb of Exyrion]] that had unleashed the [[Warp Storms]] in [[M31]].{{fn|1c}} When the [[Iron Warriors]] attack reached the squad underground, Baltus activated the orb to release a minor warp storm that ended the [[Second Battle of Exyrion]]. Surviving the event, he clawed his way to the surface and witnessed one of the [[Fallen]].{{fn|1d}}

Seeking solace in the [[Chapter]]'s rituals and not questioning what he had seen, Baltus was watched by [[Space Marine Captain|Master]] [[Seraphus]] and [[Interrogator-Chaplain]] [[Altheous]]. He was awarded a heraldic shield of a black sword on a white field and chosen as part of Altheous' team to pursue the Fallen to [[Pandrosar]].{{fn|2a}} Aboard the [[Space Hulk]] ''[[Hyberian]]'' he encountered a [[Chaos Terminator]] and [[Bloodletter]]s hunting the team in a dislocated timestream,{{fn|2b}} and was told the truth about the Fallen after he and Altheous discovered a shrine of Dark Angels [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] relics.{{fn|2c}} Upon his return to the strike force's [[Battle Barge]], Baltus began the rituals of initiation into the [[Inner Circle]].{{fn|3a}} 

Baltus succeeded in his trials, with his final trial being assigned to a mission to infiltrate [[Inquisitor]] [[Astor Sabbathiel]]'s void ship, to discover what the Inquisitor knows about the Fallen {{Fn|3b}} The squad manages to breach and board the Inquisitor's ship, encountering and killing her retinue.{{Fn|3c}} Baltus and his squad then discovered what secret the Inquisitor has been hiding: a [[daemonhost]] housing a [[Lord of Change]] named [[Sarasti]]. The daemon gloated in victory that the Dark Angels had walked right into a trap, one having been set in eons past. The daemonhost having wanted to see the entire legion fall as revenge for being defeated by [[Lion El'Jonson]] millennia ago. Baltus is shown visions of how the trap was set, sprung, and of the Dark Angels condemned by the Imperium (with a Dark Angel about to be executed by [[Roboute Guilliman]]). Baltus refuses to allow the vision to come to pass and opens fire on the daemonhost. However, his attacks only kill the host's body and free the daemon, who quickly escapes. Baltus then transmits the evidence of the inquisitor's heresy to Seraphus. Seconds later, the Fallen activates his final trap and detonates an orb (hidden in the shrine on the Pandrosar) similar to one on Exyrion, engulfing the entire Calaphrax Cluster in a warp storm. Baltus is last seen being dragged into the warp.{{Fn|3d}}

==Wargear==
Baltus wore a mixed set of Astartes [[Power Armour]], most notably wearing a [[Mk VI]] helmet. His armour was heavily damaged during the battle Exyrion, requiring heavy replacement. He received a different Mk VI helmet and pauldrons; while his greaves were originally [[Mk VII]], they were replaced with [[Mk IV]] greaves; Baltus also received a heraldic shield on his right pauldron. Baltus wielded a standard issue [[Boltgun]] in battle.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}

Bannus.wikitext:
{{IronHandsPortal}}
'''Bannus''' is a high-ranking member of the [[Iron Hands]] [[Space Marines|Space Marine]] [[chapter]]. He was wounded in a [[Dark Eldar]] ambush and has since become entombed within a [[Venerable Dreadnought]]. He is the Clan Leader of [[Clan Kaargul]] and sits on the Chapter's Clan Council.{{Fn|1}}

==Biography==
In 935.[[M41]], Bannus was severely wounded when [[Dark Eldar]] ambushed Clan Company Kaargul on the [[Industrial World]] of [[Kaladrone]]. [[Iron Father]] [[Blantar]] deemed the [[Captain]]'s loss an unacceptable blow to the strength of the Chapter and mounted a counterattack to rescue him. Despite sustaining horrific damage, Blantar and the survivors of Clan Kaargul returned to [[Medusa (Planet)|Medusa]] with Bannus's shattered body, allowing him to become entombed within a Dreadnought.{{Fn|2}}

Barabas Dantioch.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{IronWarriorsPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =Barabas_Dantioch.jpg |Caption =Barabas Dantioch{{Fn|2a}} |Title =[[Warden of the Pharos]]
Hero of the Imperium |Homeworld = |Birth =c. [[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - 009.[[M31]] |Death =009.[[M31]], [[Sotha]] |Cause of Death =Killed by [[Night Lords]] during the [[Battle of Sotha]] |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Perturabo]]
("Father" via [[gene-seed]])
[[Iron Warriors]] & Successor Warbands
("Brothers" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' *[[Warsmith]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] (Former) *Leader of the [[Sons of Dantioch]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Iron Warriors]] (Former) *[[Imperium Secundus]] **[[Sons of Dantioch]] |Notes = }} '''Barabas Dantioch''' was an [[Iron Warriors]] [[Warsmith]] assigned to the [[51st Expedition Fleet]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. He remained true to the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]] during the course of the [[Horus Heresy]].{{fn|1}} ===History=== In 999.M30, Dantioch led the Iron Warriors to bring the [[Gugann system]] to compliance. A [[Hrud]] migration through the system put a halt to that effort. Under orders from [[Perturabo]] to take the system at all costs, Dantioch ended up losing most of the legionaries under his command, several ships, and suffered an estimated three thousand years of Hrud entropy-induced aging, leaving him an old man, albeit still transhuman. The 51st Expeditionary Fleet was effectively destroyed.{{Fn|4}} He subsequently questioned Perturabo's purge of the Hrud in the region, asserting that the purge prompted the migration and inferring that Perturabo, or the Emperor himself, had made an error in committing to the campaign. His name was expunged from records and the [[Terminator armour]] intended for his use was reassigned to [[Barban Falk]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|3}} The last orders Dantioch received from Perturabo were to take the remainders of his command to [[Lesser Damantyne]] and bring it to [[compliance]] and to never show his face again.{{Fn|6}} In the process of rendering Lesser Damantyne compliant, Dantioch designed and led the construction of the [[Schadenhold]]. When [[Warsmith]] [[Idriss Krendl]] came to the fortress at the onset of the [[Horus Heresy]], ordering that it be used as a resupply point for [[Horus|Horus's]] armies, Warsmith Dantioch refused to betray the Emperor. Krendl told him that he would crush his fortress in the name of Horus.{{Fn|1}} Dantioch [[Great Siege of Lesser Damantyne|defended a bloody siege of the Schadenhold]], spending the next 366 days commanding his meager forces, who became informally known as the "[[Sons of Dantioch]]", against the 51st Expedition Fleet and the [[14th Grand Company]]. Towards the end of the siege an Nurgle-aligned [[Emperor Titan|Emperor class Titan]] was deployed against him, and managed to finally breach the fortress's defenses. With the fortress about to fall to the traitors, Dantioch gathered the surviving members of his garrison, detonated pre-set demolition charges set on structural weakpoints of the entire fortress, and teleported himself and his remaining troops onto the traitor's flagship in orbit. The destruction of the fortress' supports saw the entire structure collapse into the cavernous tunnels under the planet's surface, crashing and sinking into an immense lake of burning promethium below. The corrupted Imperator-titan and it's manible, severely wounded Warsmith Krendl, and completely destroyed the fortress along with its supply of wargear and resources. Overall destroying the traitor's objective, while having made them spend irreplaceable resources. Once onboard the traitor's flagship, Dantioch and his Iron Warriors fooled the crew into thinking they were members of the traitors, until they reached the bridge. A brief battle ensued against several members of the [[Sons of Horus]], which saw Dantioch's loyalists victorious, who then commandeered the ship for themselves. Dantioch set course for [[Terra]] with the aim of assisting the Emperor in fortifying the [[Imperial Palace]] against the traitors.{{Fn|1}} Dantioch eventually found himself on [[Sotha]], helping the [[Ultramarines]] determine the function of an ancient [[xenos]] structure underneath [[Mount Pharos]]. He also became allies with [[Alexis Polux]], overcoming Polux's reactionary hatred of the Iron Warriors by finding common ground between them. {{Fn|2x}} Through his work on the structure, known as the [[Pharos (Device)|Pharos]], he became a linchpin of [[Roboute Guilliman|Roboute Guilliman's]] [[Imperium Secundus]] due to the Pharos's ability to send not just messages, but matter across vast distances of space. He was later killed during the [[Battle of Sotha]], sacrificing his own life to thwart the [[Night Lords]] of [[Krukesh]] by overloading the Pharos after his own capture.{{Fn|4a}} Dantioch died in the arms of Polux, his former enemy mourning his fallen brother.{{Fn|4b}} ====Legacy==== Barabas Dantioch was recognized as the first [[Warden of the Pharos]] and a "'''Hero of the Imperium'''" by Guilliman's own decree. His mask remained within Mount Pharos atop the 'Aegidan Oath' sworn by [[Oberdeii]] as the new Warden of the Pharos, for almost a thousand years.{{Fn|5}} After Oberdeii became the [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Scythes of the Emperor]], the mask was removed from its resting place, becoming a badge of office for the Chapter's highest rank.{{Fn|5}}{{Fn|7a}} After the [[Fall of Sotha|Battle of Miral]], Dantioch's mask, now known as "the mask of the Warden of the Pharos", was left upon the funeral pyre of [[Chapter Master]] [[Mansirius Thorcyra]]. With Sotha wiped of life by the [[Tyranids]], a "Warden of the Pharos" was considered no longer needed.{{Fn|7b}} By [[M42]], Dantioch's story has been all but lost to legend, even among the Scythes of the Emperor. Dantioch's funeral pyre on Sotha having many myths surrounding it, "a traitor redeemed" being but one of them. The last [[Firstborn]] Chapter Master of the Scythes of the Emperor, [[Thracian (Scythes of the Emperor)|Thracian]], while not knowing who this "unknown warrior" was, believed that he would have been disappointed in the failings of the chapter.{{Fn|8}} ===Notes=== *In the [[Black Library (BL Publishing)|Black Library]] webpage for ''[[The Iron Within (Short Story)|The Iron Within]]'', the character's name is given as '''Barabaras Dantioch'''.{{Fn|9}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[The Iron Within (Short Story)]] *2: [[The Unremembered Empire]] **{{Endn|2a}}: Chapter 15 **{{Endn|2x}}: {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|3}}: [[Angel Exterminatus (Novel)]], Chapter One *4: [[Pharos (Novel)]] **{{Endn|4a}}: Chapter 29 **{{Endn|4b}}: Chapter 30 *{{Endn|5}}: [[The Aegidan Oath (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|6}}: [[Perturabo: The Hammer of Olympia (Novel)]] (e-version), pgs. 122-125 *7: [[Slaughter at Giant's Coffin (Novel)]] - [[Scythes of the Emperor (Anthology)]] **{{Endn|7a}}: Chapter Seven **{{Endn|7a}}: Chapter 12 *{{Endn|8}}: [[Belisarius Cawl: The Great Work (Novel)]], Chapter 17 *{{Endn|9}}: [https://www.blacklibrary.com/the-horus-heresy/quick-reads/iron-within-ebook.html Black Library: The Iron Within] ''(last accessed 27th September 2022)'' {{DEFAULTSORT:Dantioch, Barabas}} [[Category:Characters (Deceased)]] [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Iron Warriors)]] [[Category:Loyalists from Traitor Legions]] [[fr:Barabas Dantioch]]

{{KhornePortal}}{{CrimsonSlaughterPortal}}
[[Image:Baranox.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Baranox{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Baranox the Blood-Haunted''' was a [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] leader in the [[Crimson Slaughter]].{{Fn|1}}
==History==
Formerly a [[Veteran Sergeant]] of the [[Crimson Sabres]], he was loyal to the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]] but embraced eternal damnation with the rest of his [[Chapter]].  Baranox eventually went on to worship [[Khorne]] and led the [[Lords of Carnage]] Warband within the Crimson Slaughter.  While fighting with his Warband he also led a detachment of [[Terminator]] elite known as the [[Wrathguard]].  In his long service to the Crimson Slaughter, Baranox clashed with both the [[Space Marines]] of the [[Dark Angels]] [[Chapter]] and the [[Tyranid]]s of [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]].  He was not the type to fight at a distance, as Baranox preferred to smell his foe's spilled blood as it fell.{{Fn|1}}

During the [[13th Black Crusade|13th Black Crusade's]] invasion of [[Cadia]], Baranox killed the [[Crimson Fists]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Ruis Tracinto]]. However he died shortly afterwards, at the avenging hands of the [[Dark Angels]] [[Space Marine Captain|Master]] [[Korahael]].{{Fn|2}}

("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Warsmith]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] 126th [[Grand Company]] *Member of the [[Trident]] *[[Daemon Prince]] of [[Chaos Undivided]] |Preceded by =[[Erasmus Golg]] (As Triarch) |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Former) **[[Iron Warriors]] *[[Chaos]] **[[Chaos Undivided]] |Notes = }} '''Barban Falk''', later simply known as '''The Warsmith''', was a warlord of the [[Iron Warriors]] in late [[M41]]. ===Biography=== ====Heresy Era==== {{spoiler|source=Angel Exterminatus (Novel)}} During the [[Horus Heresy]], Barban Falk was a [[Warsmith]] of the 126th Grand Company who was part of [[Perturabo]]'s select [[Trident]] and was known for his abnormal and imposing size and strength. He was appointed to the Triarch alongside [[Kroeger]] in the aftermath of the [[First Siege of Hydra Cordatus]] and [[Battle of the Phall System]] that saw Triarchs [[Harkor]] and [[Golg]] disgraced and killed, respectively. Later it was during a [[Battle of Iydris|pitched battle]] in the depths of an [[Eldar]] tomb citadel that Falk was contacted by a daemonic entity. He used the [[warp]] presence's power to focus and command his Iron Warriors. After the escape from the Eldar tomb world of [[Iydris|Amon ny-shak Kaelis]], [[First Captain]] [[Forrix]] called Falk by name, and Falk replied, ''"I no longer know that name, I am simply the Warsmith."''{{Fn|2}} By the [[Siege of Terra]] Falk had become aloof with the concerns of the material, insisting on simply being referred to as ''The Warsmith'' and scoffing at former superiors such as Forrix. Forrix feared that, like the [[Daemon Primarch]]s, Falk's ambitions lay with [[Chaos]] and not with simple victory on Terra.{{Fn|6}} ====Post-Heresy==== [[Kalkator]]'s Grand Company operated a [[Vindicator]] siege tank named after Barban Falk.{{Fn|5}} {{spoiler|source=Storm of Iron (Novel)}} {{main|Siege of Hydra Cordatus}} In late [[M41]], "The Warsmith" was described as a powerful warrior in Daemonic armor, giving off a feeling of dread even to his hardened lieutenants.{{Fn|1a}} Leading a [[Grand Company]] to the [[Imperial]] world of [[Hydra Cordatus]], The Warsmith intended to topple the seemingly impenetrable Imperial fortress there and steal the large amount of [[Gene-Seed]] hidden within, an act he hoped would gain him enough favour with the [[Gods of Chaos]] to ascend to [[Daemonhood]].{{Fn|1b}} After a bloody battle, the Warsmith was successful in his quest and became a [[Daemon Prince]], traveling to the [[Warp]] and leaving control of his forces to his only surviving champion, [[Honsou]].{{Fn|1c}} Before his ascension, "The Warsmith" was the castellan of the fortress of [[Khalan-Ghol]] on [[Medrengard]].{{Fn|3}} In addition to his martial abilities, he was a collector of several interesting tomes of [[Chaos]] knowledge. After the fortress was destroyed, Honsou found one tome that led him to the location of the [[Daemon Prince]] [[M'kar the Reborn]].{{Fn|4}} ===Sources=== *1: [[Storm of Iron (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: Bridgehead: Part Three, pg. 51 **{{Endn|1b}}: Bridgehead: Part Four, pg. 54 **{{Endn|1c}}: Storm of Iron: Part Five, pg. 403 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Angel Exterminatus (Novel)]], Chapter 27, pg. 416. *{{Endn|3}}: [[Dead Sky, Black Sun (Novel)]], Prologue *{{Endn|4}}: [[Iron Warrior (Novella)]], Chapter One *{{Endn|5}}: [[The Last Wall (Novel)]], Chapter 12 *{{Endn|6}}: [[The First Wall (Novel)]], Chapter 2 *{{Endn|7}}: [[White Dwarf 271 (UK)]], pg. 68 {{DEFAULTSORT:Falk, Barban}} [[Category:Characters (Black Crusades)]] [[Category:Characters (Daemon)]] [[Category:Characters (Iron Warriors)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Iron Warriors (Novel Series)]]

Bardan Dovaro.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}
'''Bardan Dovaro''' was the [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Novamarines]] during the [[Indomitus Crusade]] and the [[Plague Wars]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
During the Plague Wars, Dovaro was given command of the [[Starfort]] ''[[Galatan (Star Fort)|Galatan]]'', as the [[Novamarines]] aided in defending the besieged [[Realm of Ultramar]]. However when the Star Fort was attempting to reach [[Parmenio]] to aid the efforts of [[Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]], it was boarded by the [[Death Guard]] forces of [[Typhus|Typhus the Traveller]].{{Fn|2a}} As the ''Galatan'' began to be overwhelmed, Dovaro had its defenders concentrate in protecting the Starfort's command center, to prevent the ''Galatan'' from being captured. When the Death Guard attacked it, Dovaro challenged Typhus and they dueled as their forces fought around them. At first Dovaro was overwhelming the Traveller and it appeared as if the skilled [[Chapter Master]] would be able to slay Typhus. However the Traveller was merely waiting patiently for his moment to strike and when it appeared, he fatally tore open Dovaro's chest with his [[manreaper]].{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|2c}} All seemed lost after the Chapter Masters' death, but the Death Guard were defeated after the ''Galatan'' reached Parmenio and [[Imperial]] reinforcements arrived to aid the Starfort.{{Fn|2c}} The Novamarines would later name the [[Thunderhawk]] ''[[Bardan's Fall]]'' in Dovaro's honor, which currently serves in the [[Indomitus Crusade]].{{Fn|3}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of the [[Salamanders]] [[Space Marine Legion]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

===Biography===
During the Heresy, Zytos joined the loyalist forces under [[Timur Gantulga]] and [[Eeron Kleve]] in their journey to [[Macragge]]. Upon their arrival, they discovered the seemingly dead body of [[Vulkan]]. As the Salamanders decided to bring their Primarch back to [[Nocturne]] inside the [[Unbound Flame]], Zytos thought he heard a heartbeat but dismissed it.{{Fn|2}}

Following the [[Battle of Nocturne]], Zytos was among the three Salamanders to discover the reborn [[Vulkan]] at Mt. Deathfire alongside [[Atok Abidemi]] and [[Igen Gargo]]. The three were named Vulkan's ''Draaksward'', his traveling companions on his journey through the [[Webway]] to [[Terra]]. Barek Zytos, along with Vulkan and the rest of the Draaksward, eventually reached the [[Imperial Palace]] on Terra after an arduous journey.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|2}}

Later during the [[Siege of Terra]] Zytos alongside his two battle-brothers moved to defend the Western Hemispheric region of the Palace walls from an attack by the [[Thousand Sons]]. In the subsequent battle they were aided by [[Bodvar Bjarki]] and his pack of [[Space Wolves]]. Learning from [[Lemuel Gaumon|Promeus]] that their apparent defeat of the Thousand Sons attack had just been a ruse to allow Magnus and an entourage to infiltrate the Palace.{{Fn|3a}} The group confronted Magnus and the Thousand Sons before the [[Golden Throne]].{{Fn|3b}} In the subsequent battle [[Vulkan]] dueled with the Crimson King and was about to be felled by a strike from the traitor Primarch's staff, but at the last second Zytos tackled his gene-father out of the way and took the blow instead. After the battle his sacrifice and death was remembered by Bjarki and the two surviving Salamanders who marked their armor with the head of a drake.{{Fn|3c}}

Barsabbas.wikitext:
{{CSMPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a young but famous member of the [[Blood Gorgons]] [[Chaos Space Marine]]s.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|2}}

==Overview==
{{Spoiler|source=Blood Gorgons (Novel)}}
During the Blood Gorgon [[Sorcerer]] [[Anko Muhr]]’s attempted coup against [[Gammadin]], the [[Chapter Master]] of their warband, Barsabbas was left stranded on the world of [[Hauts Bassiq]].{{Fn|1b}} On Hauts Bassiq he managed to capture the [[Dark Eldar]] [[Sindul]] whose [[Kabal]] had been working with Muhr to overthrow Gammadin.{{Fn|1c}} With the help of his Dark Eldar captive and the local human populace, Barsabbas found the imprisoned Chapter Master in the [[Hive City]] of [[Ur]].{{Fn|1f}} Together they managed to return to [[Cauldron Born]], the fortress-ship [[Space Hulk]] of the Blood Gorgons, which had been taken over by Muhr and his patron [[Chaos Lord]] [[Opsarus]].{{Fn|1g}} Barsabbas protected his master and slew the traitorous sorcerer, but he was gravely injured in the process. After the battle with Muhr, Opsarus and their forces, Barsabbas went through a long healing process and was selected as lord Gammadin’s new bond-brother.{{Fn|1h}} Gammadin’s previous bond-brother [[Sabtah]] was killed during the coup{{Fn|1d}} and Barsabbas’ previous bond-brother [[Sargaul]] was killed on Hauts Bassiq{{Fn|1e}}.

==Overview==
Covered in [[bionic]]s from a [[Plasma Gun]] malfunction, Carya had worked for years to become an officer on an [[Astartes]] ship. Commanding the [[Frigate]] ''[[Eisenstein]]'', Carya became swept up in the early stages of the [[Horus Heresy]] when his ship became the only loyalist craft to escape the [[Battle of Isstvan III]]. When loyalist leader [[Nathaniel Garro]] took command of his vessel and attempted to escape to warn [[Terra]], Carya was shocked but determined to carry out his duty. Carya proved calm and invaluable during the Eistenstein's harrowing journey through the [[Warp]], keeping discipline and command as the ship was beset by [[Daemon]]s. He survived the trip to the [[Somnus Citadel]] and it was suggested by the [[Imperial Fists]] that he may be used to train their own ship crews in the future.{{Fn|1}}

'''Basilio Fo''' was a genius biomechanical engineer who used his skills to create monstrosities that he gleefully unleashed on [[Terra]]'s population during the [[Age of Strife]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
During his life, Fo knew many of the warlords who were vying for control of [[Terra]], which included the [[Emperor]]. Fo feared the Emperor, for the Warlord was so driven that he knew that they would succeed, especially with the [[Thunder Warriors|transhuman]] [[Space Marines|warriors]] the Emperor had created. Fo developed a great hatred for these creations, fearing that with their power and numbers they could one day destroy Terra, if the Emperor were to ever lose control of them. Fo also believed that, in the Emperor's arrogance and pride, he would subjugate Terra's population in pursuit of his vision once he had defeated his enemies. Those that resisted his [[Imperium]] would be dealt with and Fo wanted no part in either outcome. By then, Fo had been labeled a criminal for the deaths caused by his monsters and he feared that he would be caught and brought to justice by the Emperor. In order to ensure that never happened, Fo fled Terra aboard a ship and escaped beyond the Emperor's reach.{{Fn|1a}} 

Fo had long ago used his by biomechanical skills to significantly extend his lifespan, so he was able to survive the journey that led to the world [[Velich Tarn]]. He would go on to rule the world, untroubled by anyone, until Velich Tarn was discovered by the [[Primarch]] [[Horus]]'s [[63rd Expeditionary Fleet]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. Horus sought to bring Velich Tarn into compliance with the [[Imperium]], but Fo resisted and defended his world. In the battle that followed, Fo's skills and monsters nearly killed the Primarch before Horus defeated him. Instead of being killed, however, Fo was captured and sent back to [[Terra]], where he was imprisoned in the [[Imperial Dungeon]]. His defeat caused Fo to develop a great hatred of Horus and he spent his imprisonment thinking of various ways to kill the Primarch.{{Fn|1b}}

During the [[Siege of Terra]], Fo was visited by [[Amon Tauromachian]], [[Kyril Sindermann]], and [[Euphrati Keeler]] as part of the efforts of the new [[Order of Interrogation]]. During these interviews, Fo claimed that he could create a virus capable of killing not only all [[Space Marine]]s, but also the [[Primarch]]s. Seeing the possibility to save Terra, Amon allowed Sindermann and Keeler to look into the feasibility of aiding Fo in creating such a weapon.{{Fn|1c}}

Continually interrogated by Keeler, Sindermann, Amon, and the Prison Warden [[Vaskale]], Fo slowly revealed his knowledge upon a [[data-slate]]. However, this was a deliberate delaying tactic in order to gain access to Warden Vaskale and slowly implant him with linguistic voice suggestions. In truth, Fo could have revealed his knowledge over mere hours. Gathering a shard of [[Noctilith|Blackstone]], Fo sought to make his escape but was confronted by the [[Selenar]] Priestess [[Andromeda-17]], who revealed that she had taken control of Vaskale herself. Fo expected to be killed due to the ancient hatred the Selenar had toward him, but instead he was set free.{{Fn|2a}}

Now roaming the Palace and managing to elude even the [[Custodes]], Fo sought to set up a laboratory to bring about his great weapon.{{Fn|3a}} However he was instead captured and grievously wounded by a roaming [[Night Lord]], who knew of his identity thanks to his [[Daemon]]ic pacts.{{Fn|3b}} The Night Lord decided Fo was too dangerous to be left alive, but as he was about to be slain the mad scientist was saved by [[Constantin Valdor]], who brought him back to the [[Bhab Bastion]].{{Fn|3c}}

After Valdor captured Fo again, he was handed back to Amon's custody. During the final hours of the Siege as Valdor, Dorn, and the Emperor are off fighting Horus aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', Amon received a summons to hand Fo over to [[Wardens of the Sodality of the Key|Custodian Wardens]].{{Fn|4a}} As Amon escorted Fo to what was likely execution, the mad scientist ground away at Amon's confidence in the order by questioning its validity. As Amon was about to hand over Fo to the Wardens, Fo was able to get his would-be executioners to admit they could not confirm the validation of their custody order. This caused the two sides to nearly come to blows, and Amon stormed back off with Fo until such a time that the execution order could be affirmed. Amon and Fo then ran into [[Zaranchek Xanthus]] and [[Andromeda-17]], who accompanied them to an office of the Sigillite.{{Fn|4b}} Fo, Xanthus, and Andromeda-17 next journeyed to the [[Sigillite's Retreat]] to use Malcador's lab to create a perfected version of his bio-weapon that had no chance of mutating to also infect non-Astartes.{{Fn|5}}

After Fo completed his work, he ambushed an unsuspecting Xanthus and murdered him with a surgical scalpel.{{Fn|6a}} Fo was then able to use his earlier samples from Xanthus to rapidly clone a replacement body and somehow inhabit it, while Fo's originally body was hunted down and killed by Amon.{{Fn|6b}} With Fo thought dead, the mad scientist took on Zaranchek Xanthus's identity.{{Fn|6c}}

By [[M32]], Zaranchek Xanthus was a [[Radical]] [[Inquisitor]]. Accused of Chaos worship, he maintained that he remained pure but merely used the forces of the Warp to better mankind. It was his firm stance that such power could be harnessed without spiritual corruption. However, despite this defense, Xanthus was ultimately burnt at the stake for heresy. Nonetheless his ideology lives on in the Radical philosophy [[Xanthism]].{{Fn|7}}

Bastarnae Abranxe.wikitext:
{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion's]] [[85th Company (Emperor's Children)|85th Company]], during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}}

Shortly after the [[Dropsite Massacre]], Abranxe was among the Legion's [[Brotherhood of the Phoenix]], who came to a meeting called by Captain [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] and were convinced by him that a [[Daemon]] has possessed their [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]].  Incensed at the idea{{Fn|1a}}, the Brotherhood devised a plan to ambush the Primarch aboard the [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Andronicus]]'', when Fulgrim was due to visit the lab of [[Chief Apothecary]] [[Fabius]]{{Fn|1b}}, and then find a way to force the Daemon to leave his body{{Fn|1a}}.  However, during the ambush, Fulgrim proved himself to be a deadly opponent, despite being vastly outnumbered and seriously wounded Abranxe.  Though the ambush was successful{{Fn|1c}}, Abranxe's body had to be biologically restored by Fabius and Fulgrim was tortured to free him of the Daemon's control.  However, the Primarch quickly revealed that his capture had been a ruse and easily freed himself{{Fn|1d}}.  The Primarch admitted that while his body had been controlled by a Daemon, which happened after Fulgrim's shock at killing his brother [[Ferrus Manus]], this had allowed him to come to a better understanding of the powers given to him by his worship of [[Slaanesh]].  This later allowed the Primarch to retake control of his body and Fulgrim stated that he was now ready, to share the secrets he had learned with his Legion.{{Fn|1f}}

Abranxe was later killed in a boarding action; while the Emperor's Children were attempting to take the [[Iron Hands]] [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Sisypheum]]'', he attempted to interfere in a duel between [[Lucius (Emperor's Children)|Lucius]] and [[Nykona Sharrowkyn]].  As a result, Sharrowkyn beheaded him, doing enough damage to his body that Lucius thought not even Fabius would be able to bring him back afterwards.{{Fn|2}}

{{EcclesiarchyPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Heretic]] and madman who worshiped [[Daemons]] of fire and air, until he renounced his faith after embracing the worship of the [[Emperor]], which helped him regain his sanity. He then became renowned for performing the '''Miracle of the Maimed Souls''', which helped to heal those whose spirits had become damaged by traumatic experiences or mental illness. Bastian continued to do this for some time until his death, when he was struck nine times by [[bolter]] rounds. However, he would be declared an [[Imperial Saint]] after his death and was canonized as '''Saint Bastion Apostate'''; while the [[Ecclesiarchy]] further honoured his Sainthood, by establishing a hospice on [[Symbal Iota]]. Named the '''Hospice of Saint Bastian Apostate''', the staff there provide care, both physically and spiritually, for members of the military, who have been driven insane by their experiences fighting the [[Imperium]]'s many enemies.{{Fn|1}}

Bastille the Seventh.wikitext:
{{QuoteBox |quote = '''''Indigenous natives, you say? Run out the forward batteries, Commander Mieland, and let's show them how the Imperial Navy negotiates.'''''
''Lord-Admiral Bastille, in orbit of the [[Maiden World]] of [[Fionnadh]]{{Fn|1d}} |}}
'''Lord-Admiral Bastille the Seventh''' is a [[Rogue Trader]] who operated in the [[Koronus Expanse]] in late [[M41]]. ==Biography== Bastille was a very minor scion of an ancient Rogue Trader household, who was so far down the line of succession that not a single member of his house would ever have believed that he'd come to be it's patriarch. Instead, his family purchased him a commission in the [[Imperial Navy]] as soon as he was old enough to take on the responsibility, seeing it as being a better career prospect for him.{{Fn|1a}} Bastille made both friends and enemies whilst in [[Battlefleet Obscurus]],{{Fn|1a}} but managed to rise up high enough to at least captain his own ship.{{Fn|1b}} It's unclear whether he became a Lord-Admiral whilst in the Navy, or whether it was a title that he took for himself after the event that thrust him into power. A malfunction during a conference of Bastille's senior household leadership caused a stock of [[vortex torpedo]]es to detonate, killing every single member of the house in attendance, leaving Bastille as the most senior member of the Rogue Trader house left. He resigned his Naval commission immediately, and took his house's [[Warrant of Trade]] for himself, renaming the house to [[House Bastille]] in his own honour.{{Fn|1a}} His enemies in the Navy pursued him for years after his resignation, spreading awful rumours about the man without actually making any accusations that he could legally respond to. Bastille couldn't let this insult stand, and the battle of words eventually lead to his assembled enemies using their Navy ships to go into open conflict with House Bastille. It was only thanks to Bastille's remaining friends in the Navy that [[Segmentum Obscurus|Segmentum Command]] at [[Cypra Mundi]] never learned of the details of the isolated war, but it was determined that Bastille should keep out of the way of the Navy from that point on.{{Fn|1a}} In late M41, Bastille and his Rogue Trader fleet would arrive at [[Footfall]], looking for the treasure planet known as the [[Fionnadh|Dread Pearl]] somewhere in the [[Koronus Expanse]]. While looking for the Dread Pearl, Bastille came into conflict with a fellow Rogue Trader, Lady [[Sun Lee]], the Matriarch of the House of [[Ma'Kao]], after he caught one of her raiders spying on his fleet in the [[Delectus Nox]] system and badly damaged it in the ensuing skirmish.{{Fn|1c}} ==Personality== Bastille didn't lend himself well to creating allies, instead preferring subordinates who could follow orders. He had a shoot first and ask questions later attitude, but also possessed a deeply entrenched sense of military honour, considering tactics involving subterfuge as mean-spirited and dishonourable. Many suspected that he orchestrated the vortex torpedo malfunction that killed the senior members of his Rogue Trader house, but that would have been quite out of character for the man. ==Equipment== Bastille wore a reinforced captain's uniform that fully covered his [[bionic]] arm and leg. He wielded a powerful naval-pattern [[stub pistol]] and a [[power maul]] in combat.{{Fn|1b}} ==Sources== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Rogue Trader: Lure of the Expanse]] **{{Endn|1a}}: I: Eye of the Needle, pg. 27 **{{Endn|1b}}: Appendix: NPCs, pgs. 124-125 **{{Endn|1c}}: II: The Heathen Trail, pgs. 55-56 **{{Endn|1d}}: III: The World Beyond, pg. 112 [[Category:Characters (Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Imperial Navy)]] [[Category:Characters (Rogue Traders)]]
